title: AutoLR: Automating the Path from Research to Launch Review in Industrial Recommender Systems
abstract: Improving an industrial recommender is an iterative research-and-engineering process rather than a direct path from idea to deployment. In \textbf{DASHEN, NetEase's gaming-community app}, algorithm engineers typically identify promising directions from research papers, technical reports, and prior production experiments; reproduce or adapt the underlying methods; implement them in the production codebase; and evaluate the resulting models through training and offline experiments. Promising candidates are then advanced to online A/B tests, and those demonstrating robust gains are submitted to Launch Review---the internal gate for full-traffic rollout. Large language models (LLMs) can assist with individual stages of this workflow, but the overall process remains human-dependent without a harness that can reliably coordinate them across long-running, often multi-day experimental cycles. We present \textbf{AutoLR}, initially built as \textbf{Auto Launch Review} and later extended upstream into an autonomous research-to-launch harness. AutoLR combines three system mechanisms: a \textbf{multi-expert council} that debates and adversarially reviews proposals; a \textbf{deterministic evidence-weighted exploration--exploitation selector} that allocates a limited trial budget across candidate directions and uses Council reranking; and a layered knowledge system that combines external research, production-system knowledge, and DASHEN-specific domain knowledge---such as game communities, player characteristics, and content-interaction patterns---with posterior evidence from configurations, patches, logs, failures, and offline outcomes. LLM agents perform semantic reasoning and code generation, while deterministic controllers retain authority over execution, metric extraction, guardrails, and persistent state transitions.

title: AI CHATBOT FOR COLLEGE STUDENT SERVICES
authors: 1Yamini Chouhan, 2 G sahana, 3 K Navadeep, 4 M Nikhil, 5 R Kamalakar
abstract: The AI Chatbot for College Student Services is an intelligent system designed to provide students with quick, convenient, and automated access to important collegerelated information and services. Students often need information regarding courses, class schedules, examinations, attendance, fees, departments, faculty, events, campus facilities, and academic procedures. Traditional methods of obtaining such information may require students to visit administrative offices, contact faculty members, or search through different college resources, which can be time-consuming. The proposed chatbot provides a centralized conversational interface through which students can obtain relevant information using simple natural language queries. The system uses Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to understand student questions and provide appropriate responses. It can identify the intent of a students query, process the available college information, and return relevant answers through a conversational interface. The chatbot can be designed to handle frequently asked questions, provide academic and administrative information, guide students to appropriate departments, and assist with common college services. The main objective of the proposed system is to improve accessibility to college information while reducing the workload of administrative staff. The chatbot can provide responses quickly and can be made available throughout the day, allowing students to access information without depending entirely on office working hours. It also provides a consistent method of delivering frequently requested information.

title: Progressive Reinforcement Learning for Whole-Body Humanoid Manipulation
abstract: Humanoidni roboti so zasnovani za delo v okoljih, prilagojenih ljudem, zato je manipulacija z usklajenim gibanjem celotnega telesa, hkratno upravljanje rok in nog za doseganje, prijemanje in manipulacijo predmetov, ena izmed ključnih nalog sodobne robotike. Učenje takšnih nalog z metodami spodbujevalnega učenja je zahtevno zaradi kompleksnosti visokodimenzionalnega prostora akcij in kompleksnih nagrad, še posebej kadar so vse nagrade vključene hkrati, saj agent namesto postopnega osvajanja posameznih veščin sklepa kompromise med nasprotujočimi si cilji in konvergira k slabemu lokalnemu minimumu. Glavni cilj tega dela je učenje strategije za stabilno manipulacijo predmeta s humanoidnim robotom, ki temelji na usklajenem gibanju celotnega telesa, pri čemer se mora robot naučiti učinkovitega izvajanja naloge ob hkratnem zagotavljanju stabilnosti in ravnotežja. Za reševanje tega problema je uporabljen progresivni pristop: naloga je razdeljena na tri zaporedne faze učenja, pri čemer vsaka faza nadgradi naučeno vedenje iz prejšnje faze z novimi funkcijami nagrade. Robot Talos je bil najprej naučen vzdrževati ravnotežje ob zunanjih motnjah, nato segati po predmetu na mizi in nazadnje predmet stisniti ter dvigniti. Učenje poteka v simulacijskem okolju IsaacLab z uporabo metode spodbujevalnega učenja, pri čemer je za optimizacijo strategije uporabljen algoritem PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization). Rezultati potrjujejo učinkovitost progresivnega pristopa, saj je robot uspešno usvojil zaporedne faze učenja, od vzdrževanja ravnotežja do izvajanja manipulacijske naloge. V končni fazi je robot uspešno izvedel prijem in dvig predmeta, pri čemer pristop kaže potencial za učenje kompleksnega vedenja z usklajenim gibanjem celotnega telesa pri humanoidnih robotih.

title: Eidolon-S: Experimental Code for Minimal Self-Awareness Emergence Study
abstract: This repository contains the full experimental code for the paper *Emergence Conditions and Robustness Verification of Minimal Self-Awareness: A Systematic Study Based on Controlled Ablation Experiments*. The code implements the Eidolon‑S silicon-based self-interested life form simulation platform, and covers all 12 groups of controlled experiments reported in the paper:- Condition ablation experiments (boundary irreversibility, boundary vulnerability, conflict dimension, network architecture)- F0 training step calibration experiment- N-Probe latent space representation analysis- Goal-driven life form control experiments (5 parametric subgroups)- Causal controllability deprivation experiments- Gradient deprivation-reconstruction experiments- Methodological robustness verification (threshold scanning, hyperparameter perturbation, survivorship bias correction) All experiments strictly follow the single-variable control principle. The code can be used to reproduce all experimental results and statistical conclusions in the original paper. If you use this code in your research, please cite the original paper.

title: Title: Fractal Field Theory for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Fractal Field Theory (FFT) offers a novel approach to quantum error correction, moving beyond traditional linear algebra-based methods. This paper explores the application of FFT to represent and mitigate quantum errors, hypothesizing that quantum states can be modeled as fractal distributions, facilitating efficient error detection and correction through pattern recognition and fractal-based algorithms. The core claim is that FFT can significantly enhance the robustness of quantum computation by addressing the computational bottlenecks associated with existing error correction techniques. We present a theoretical framework outlining the mathematical foundations of FFT-based error correction and demonstrate its potential for practical implementation. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications of this approach for quantum information processing.

title: 基于图的强化学习的策略梯度优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to reinforcement learning, termed "Graph-Based Strategic Gradient Optimization" (GBGSO), that leverages graph-based representations of the environment to facilitate automated strategy gradient adjustment. Traditional reinforcement learning often relies on static policies, limiting their adaptability to dynamic environments. GBGSO dynamically adjusts the graph structure surrounding each state, optimizing the policy gradients directly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through extensive experiments on several challenging reinforcement learning tasks, showcasing significant improvements in learning speed and final performance compared to existing strategies. The core mechanism involves constructing a graph where states are nodes, and actions are edges, with an adaptive gradient adjustment process applied to the graph topology. This adaptive adjustment allows the algorithm to better navigate complex environments and discover optimal policies. We present a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, highlighting its advantages in handling complex state spaces and dynamic environments.

title: Probability Space Quantum Entanglement Simulator
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic space quantum entanglement simulator designed to efficiently model and simulate complex quantum entanglement states. Traditional quantum computation approaches often struggle with the inherent complexity of entangled states. This paper proposes a new algorithm that leverages a probability distribution to model entangled states, enabling direct calculation of entanglement probabilities rather than relying on complex quantum calculations. The core mechanism involves mapping the quantum state to a probability distribution, then using this distribution to simulate the evolution of the entangled state. This approach offers a significant improvement in computational efficiency and the potential for enhanced quantum algorithm capabilities. The paper details the design of this simulator, its performance evaluation, and its implications for future quantum computing advancements.

title: 基于量子纠缠的拓扑计算 (QCT) 算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing algorithm, the "基于量子纠缠的拓扑计算" (QCT) algorithm, designed to facilitate the study and simulation of complex topological structures. The core concept of the QCT algorithm leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to accelerate and enhance the discovery of novel topological phenomena. We detail the algorithm's structure, mechanisms, and potential applications, emphasizing its ability to circumvent the limitations of traditional computational approaches. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's theoretical foundations and preliminary experimental validation, highlighting its promise for advancing the field of topological computation.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Computation Paradigm
abstract: Quantum Entanglement-Based Computation Paradigm is a novel approach to computation that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to achieve significantly enhanced computational efficiency compared to classical approaches. This paper explores the fundamental principles of entanglement, its role in quantum mechanics, and the design of a computational paradigm centered around this phenomenon. The core mechanism involves utilizing entangled states to facilitate data manipulation, entanglement-based algorithms, and a novel method for information transfer, ultimately aiming to overcome the limitations of classical computation. We present a conceptual framework outlining the potential benefits and challenges associated with this paradigm, emphasizing its promise for revolutionizing computational capabilities.

title: Geometric Information Theory: Adaptive Topology Transformation & Quantum Algorithm Fusion
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid algorithm combining adaptive topology transformation with quantum algorithms to achieve high-precision geometric transformations and calculations. Traditional geometric transformation methods rely on fixed topologies, while this approach leverages the adaptive transformation capabilities of geometric information theory to enable more flexible and efficient computations. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a carefully designed transformation process, guided by geometric information, which is enhanced by the inherent computational advantages of quantum algorithms. We present a theoretical framework outlining the algorithm's architecture and discuss its potential impact on various geometric computation problems. The study aims to advance the field of geometric computation by exploring a new paradigm for achieving high-precision transformations.

title: Dynamic Topology of Quantum Probability Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic topology to quantum probability models, aiming to enhance quantum system capabilities through adaptive probability distributions. We present a novel framework that dynamically adjusts probability distributions based on quantum system states and environmental influences. The core mechanism relies on the construction of dynamic topology, allowing for automated optimization of probability distributions tailored to the system's characteristics. The work demonstrates a significant improvement in computational performance and system adaptability compared to traditional approaches. This research contributes to a deeper understanding of the potential for dynamic topology to revolutionize quantum computation.

title: Quantum Biofeedback Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to complex system control and optimization utilizing a Quantum Biofeedback Algorithm. The core concept involves simulating quantum biofeedback mechanisms within a computational framework, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to construct a model mirroring biological feedback loops. Quantum bits (qubits) represent biological signals, and quantum gates simulate the transmission and regulation inherent in these loops. This approach aims to achieve precise control over target systems characterized by high non-linearity. The algorithm's novelty lies in its fusion of quantum computing principles with biological feedback mechanisms, offering a potential solution beyond the limitations of conventional control theories. The methodology presented herein provides a theoretical framework and a potential pathway for addressing intricate problems with highly non-linear characteristics.

title: Variable Parameter Neural Morphological Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neural morphological computing architecture centered around a dynamically adjustable parameter control mechanism. Traditional neural morphological computing architectures often suffer from fixed parameters, limiting their computational efficiency and adaptability. This work addresses this limitation by introducing an adaptive feedback control system that continuously monitors and adjusts the parameters within the architecture based on the computational results. The core mechanism involves establishing a closed-loop system where the output of a computation influences the adjustment of the underlying parameters, ultimately optimizing the architecture's performance for specific tasks. The system's ability to adapt in real-time offers significant potential for improved computational efficiency and robustness compared to static architectures. The theoretical framework and the proposed control strategy are presented, highlighting the key elements for achieving dynamic optimization in neural morphological computing. The focus is on the design principles and the potential impact of this adaptive approach on various computational applications.

title: Cloze-Scale-75 & LLM-DNA: Multi-Corpus Forensic Benchmark Dataset for Prober Parameter Dynamics, Context Bounding, and AI Text Attribution
abstract: ### 1. Dataset Overview & ScopeThis open-access repository contains the official benchmark corpora, multi-model evaluation traces, and cryptographically verified forensic audit trails supporting the research paper:*"The Cloze Scaling Laws: Prober Parameter Dynamics, Native Blank-Infilling Architecture, and Discourse Context Bounding in Large Language Models"*. This dataset establishes standard benchmark splits for evaluating zero-shot macroscopic cloze infilling detectors, model parameter scaling laws (12B to 120B), context deprivation bounds in low-resource abstracts, and multi-model latent DNA attribution. --- ### 2. Included Benchmark Corpora & Splits The dataset bundle contains **75 verified evaluation samples** across four core scientific sub-corpora: 1. **RAID Curated Benchmark (`raid_benchmark_curated.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: ACL 2024 Adversarial AI Text Benchmark. - **Focus**: Dense, short single-paragraph abstracts ($n \le 6$ sentences) written by adversarial generators vs. human scientists. - **Target**: Evaluates discourse context deprivation bounds and zero-shot recovery under severe structural constraints. 2. **HC3 Curated Q&A Corpus (`hc3_benchmark_curated.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: Human vs. ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (EMNLP 2023). - **Focus**: Technical, biomedical, and financial question-answering pairs across human subject experts vs. GPT-3.5/GPT-4. - **Target**: Evaluates semantic congruence and conversational register shifts. 3. **Academic Multi-Domain Corpus (`paper1_academic_benchmark.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: Formal peer-reviewed academic literature across 6 domains (Physics, Macroeconomics, Epistemology, Systems, Psychology, Ecology). - **Target**: Establishes rigorous human specificity ($0\%$ FPR bounds) against frontier LLM generations. 4. **Project Gutenberg Classic Literature (`gutenberg_human_literature.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: Public domain human classic literature. - **Target**: Controls for historical lexical diversity, sentence length burstiness, and stylistic invariance. 5. **Multi-Model 6-Class Attribution Tournament Corpus (`corpus/essay_*.txt`)**: - **Origin**: 30 long-form academic essays generated across 6 distinct leading model architectures: OpenAI (GPT-4o), Anthropic (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), Google (Gemini 1.5 Pro / 2.5 Flash), DeepSeek (R1), Meta (Llama 3.3 70B), and Human Academic Baseline. - **Target**: Forensic provenance attribution and self-model resonance tournament. --- ### 3. Data Schema & File Structure #### JSONL Format:Each sample in the curated benchmark corpora follows this standard JSON schema:```json{ "id": "raid_ai_sample_01", "domain": "Biomedical Engineering", "text": "... [Full sample text] ...", "ground_truth": "ai", // "ai" or "human" "generator_model": "gpt-4o", // Source architecture or null for human "length_tokens": 184, "sentence_count": 6, "content_sha256": "4a7f9b..." // Cryptographic SHA-256 fingerprint}

Included Benchmark Corpora & Splits The dataset bundle contains **75 verified evaluation samples** across four core scientific sub-corpora: 1. **RAID Curated Benchmark (`raid_benchmark_curated.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: ACL 2024 Adversarial AI Text Benchmark. - **Focus**: Dense, short single-paragraph abstracts ($n \le 6$ sentences) written by adversarial generators vs. human scientists. - **Target**: Evaluates discourse context deprivation bounds and zero-shot recovery under severe structural constraints. 2. **HC3 Curated Q&A Corpus (`hc3_benchmark_curated.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: Human vs. ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (EMNLP 2023). - **Focus**: Technical, biomedical, and financial question-answering pairs across human subject experts vs. GPT-3.5/GPT-4. - **Target**: Evaluates semantic congruence and conversational register shifts. 3. **Academic Multi-Domain Corpus (`paper1_academic_benchmark.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: Formal peer-reviewed academic literature across 6 domains (Physics, Macroeconomics, Epistemology, Systems, Psychology, Ecology). - **Target**: Establishes rigorous human specificity ($0\%$ FPR bounds) against frontier LLM generations. 4. **Project Gutenberg Classic Literature (`gutenberg_human_literature.jsonl`)**: - **Origin**: Public domain human classic literature. - **Target**: Controls for historical lexical diversity, sentence length burstiness, and stylistic invariance. 5. **Multi-Model 6-Class Attribution Tournament Corpus (`corpus/essay_*.txt`)**: - **Origin**: 30 long-form academic essays generated across 6 distinct leading model architectures: OpenAI (GPT-4o), Anthropic (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), Google (Gemini 1.5 Pro / 2.5 Flash), DeepSeek (R1), Meta (Llama 3.3 70B), and Human Academic Baseline. - **Target**: Forensic provenance attribution and self-model resonance tournament. --- ### 3. title: Quantum Entangled State Adaptive Correction Code Design
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers unprecedented opportunities for information processing and secure communication, but inherent vulnerabilities exist due to its sensitivity to environmental noise. This paper investigates the design of a novel quantum entanglement-based adaptive correction code, leveraging the inherent properties of quantum states to enhance error correction and information preservation. We propose a dynamic correction parameter system, enabling the code to dynamically adjust to quantum state distortions. This approach contrasts with traditional approaches reliant on static parameters, promising improved resilience against environmental interference. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the code's effectiveness in mitigating quantum decoherence. The core claim is that this quantum entanglement-based adaptive correction code offers a significant advancement in error correction compared to existing methods, particularly in the face of complex and dynamic quantum environments.

title: Dynamic Quantum Hidden Matrix (DQM)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Quantum Hidden Matrix (DQM) algorithm, a novel approach to quantum computation that dynamically adjusts matrix parameters based on input data. The DQM aims to enhance the efficiency and robustness of quantum algorithms by eliminating the need for fixed, pre-defined parameters. The algorithm's core mechanism involves iterative refinement of matrix elements, guided by a feedback loop that continuously optimizes for desired performance characteristics. This approach offers a potential paradigm shift in quantum computing, addressing limitations of traditional methods and opening up new avenues for algorithm design. This research explores the theoretical foundations, implementation details, and initial experimental results demonstrating the DQM's effectiveness in a specific quantum computing task.

title: Scientific Computing Applications of Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph theory offers an influential foundation for interpreting, understating, and modeling neural network models. Graphs are very effective in grasping the complex connections in neural networks. Starting from representing the neurons, synapses and the weight matrix, the notions of graph theory are essential in every aspect of neural network modeling and analysis. This synergism has sparked off to design Graph Neural Networks (GNN), a specialized neural network to process graph-structured data. GNN has arisen as an efficient means for analyzing and predicting complex systems in numerous arenas of scientific computing. These networks support combinatorial generalization and relational reasoning. They lay the strong foundation for better interpretable, flexible, and sophisticated patterns of reasoning. This chapter delivers a big picture of the applications of GNNs in various fields like computer science, material science, physics, biology, and chemistry. For instance, GNNs can be beneficial in computer science in areas like computer vision tasks, natural language processing tasks and recommendation systems. It can predict properties of materials and formulate new materials with specific desired properties in the field of material science. In physics, it is applied to study quantum many-body systems, condensed matter physics, high-energy physics and to speculate their behavior and properties. GNNs are useful to predict molecular properties, to formulate new molecules with desired properties and to predict the products of chemical reactions. In biology, GNNs are applied to analyze the protein function and structure, to predict gene expression levels and to analyze cellular networks and their behavior. This chapter brings out the impression of the fascinating tool, GNN in various fields enlightening with the scientific computing applications. It also highlights the key research findings and provides resources for further investigation of GNNs.

title: Diffusion TV: Experiencing Diffusion Models through Tangible, Embodied Interaction
abstract: Diffusion TV is an interactive AI art installation that offers a tangible and embodied experience of diffusion models through a modified CRT TV. By physically manipulating the TV's antenna, audiences control the clarity of AI-generated images and sounds, metaphorically enacting the denoising process that underlies diffusion-based generation. Using the tuning knob, participants switch between three channels featuring AI-generated animals from the Past (extinct species), Present (endangered species), and Future (speculative creatures), situating the interaction within a temporal and ecological narrative. Through continuous audiovisual feedback and physical interaction, Diffusion TV foregrounds the generative process over final outputs, allowing audiences to explore intermediate states as experiential material. Rather than providing explicit technical explanation, the work presents an alternative, embodied mode of explainable AI that invites exploratory engagement with and reflection on generative technologies.

title: Cross-dataset transportability of pediatric chest X-ray deep learning across three countries: discrimination, calibration, operating-point failure, and limited-label recovery
abstract: Background and Objective: External evaluation of medical-imaging AI is often collapsed into discrimination. We evaluated a computational protocol that separately tests discrimination, probability calibration, fixed operatingpoint transport, shortcut-associated signal, and limited-label recoverability for pediatric pneumonia classification across datasets from three countries. Methods: After exact-duplicate removal, 5,824 Guangzhou radiographs supported leakage-controlled source development and internal testing. A frozen three-seed DenseNet121 dual-view ensemble was evaluated zero-shot on BDCXR-3257 from Bangladesh (n = 3, 257) and an untouched harmonized VinDr-PCXR/PediCXR test cohort from Vietnam (n = 1, 077). Matched seed-42 variants tested architectural robustness. Secondary BDCXR analyses used a fixed 651-image adaptation pool and 2,606-image hold-out; 163, 326, and 651 labels represented 5%, 10%, and 20% of complete BDCXR. Results: Internal AUROC was 0.976 with 95.1% sensitivity. BDCXR and VinDr-PCXR AUROC were 0.798 and 0.742, while frozen-threshold sensitivity fell to 6.2% and 0%. Source-to-BDCXR AUROC degradation occurred for a full-image baseline (0.961 to 0.749), ungated dual-view model (0.977 to 0.766), and gated MixStyle model (0.966 to 0.789). With 163 BDCXR labels, Platt recalibration preserved AUROC while increasing held-out sensitivity to 88.3%, but specificity was 47.9% and the alert rate was 78.5%. Two hundred repeated 163-label fits confirmed sensitivity recovery but substantial specificity variability. Conclusions: Cross-dataset shifts across countries affected ranking, probability alignment, and source-defined decision behavior differently. Transport studies should evaluate these components separately and quantify the operational burden of apparent recovery.

title: Qmes: Quantum Meta-Learning for Encoding Selection in Quantum Kernel Methods
abstract: Selecting an effective encoding quantum circuit is a key challenge in quantum kernel methods because different feature maps can lead to different performance. Conventional methods require constructing and evaluating every circuit for each new dataset, making it computationally expensive. We present Qmes, an open-source Python package that automatically recommends circuits through meta-learning. Qmes characterizes a dataset using classical complexity measures and queries a pre-trained model to recommend circuits without quantum evaluation at inference time. The package provides modular components for meta-feature extraction, quantum-kernel evaluation, recommender training, model selection, and user-defined circuit extension. We validate Qmes on 105 classification and 86 regression benchmark datasets. Qmes reduces the mean recommendation regret by 2.2x and 4.2x for classification and regression, respectively, compared to a non-adaptive baseline, with statistical significance confirmed via a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test ($p < 10^{-4}$). Qmes thus enables efficient and practical encoding-circuit selection for quantum kernel methods.

title: AI BASED LANGUAGE TRANSLATOR
authors: 1T Manasa, 2 U Keerthana, 3 V Rakesh, 4 Mena Kiran, 5 T Kalyani Devi
abstract: The AI-Based Language Translator is an intelligent system designed to overcome language barriers by providing fast, accurate, and convenient translation between multiple languages. Communication across different languages can be challenging in education, business, travel, healthcare, and everyday interactions. Traditional translation methods may require human translators or separate translation tools, which can be time-consuming and difficult to access. The proposed system uses Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Machine Learning techniques to understand and translate text from one language into another. The system allows users to enter or provide text in a selected source language and choose a target language for translation. The input text is processed using NLP techniques to understand words, phrases, sentence structure, and contextual meaning before generating the translated output. The system can support multiple languages and provide translations through a simple and user-friendly interface. Additional features such as language detection, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and translation history can also be integrated to improve accessibility and usability. The main objective of the proposed system is to provide an efficient and intelligent translation solution that can assist users in communicating across different languages. By applying AI-based language processing techniques, the system aims to improve translation quality while reducing the time and effort required for manual translation. Overall, the AI-Based Language Translator provides a centralized platform for multilingual communication and can be further enhanced to support more languages, voice translation, real-time conversation, and context-aware translation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Information Extraction Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing information processing and analysis. This research investigates a novel algorithm, the Quantum Entanglement Topological Information Extraction Algorithm, designed to efficiently extract topological information from complex systems. Traditional approaches often rely on classical measurement, limiting their potential for truly comprehensive data extraction. We propose a method leveraging the instantaneous correlation inherent in entangled states to precisely measure system topology and subsequently derive interpretable rules. This algorithm offers a fundamentally new path towards highly efficient and precise topological information retrieval.

title: Title: Adaptive Complexity Networks (ACN) for Computational Physics
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Complexity Networks (ACN) as a novel architecture for computational physics simulations, specifically designed to improve efficiency and robustness in complex systems. Traditional network designs often struggle with the inherent complexity of input data, necessitating manual parameter adjustments. ACN dynamically adapts the network's complexity based on the input data, creating a self-modifying system that optimizes performance. We present a comprehensive theoretical analysis and experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of ACN in various simulation scenarios. The core mechanism involves an iterative optimization process that adjusts network parameters to enhance data processing and minimize errors. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this architecture for broader computational physics applications.

title: Core Claim: Design a method for quantum entanglement computation-based self-adaptive topology assessment, utilizing the adaptive properties of entangled states to evaluate quantum computing topology, thereby improving computational efficiency.
abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary paradigm shift in computation, relies heavily on the manipulation and understanding of quantum states, particularly entanglement. The exploration and analysis of quantum entanglement – the correlation of two or more quantum systems – is a crucial aspect of quantum algorithm development and verification. Current methods for assessing quantum topology, essential for understanding and optimizing quantum circuits, often rely on static, predetermined parameters. These static approaches struggle to adapt to the dynamic and complex nature of quantum systems, hindering efficient algorithm design and testing. This paper introduces a novel method for quantum entanglement computation-based self-adaptive topology assessment, aiming to overcome this limitation. The proposed framework utilizes the inherent adaptive properties of entangled states to dynamically adjust computation parameters, providing a more robust and efficient evaluation of quantum computing topology. Specifically, it employs a self-tuning mechanism that adjusts the quantum circuit's parameters based on the observed entanglement properties, thereby minimizing computational overhead while maintaining high fidelity. The core mechanism involves a dynamic parameter adjustment strategy that reacts to the observed entanglement correlations, improving the algorithm's accuracy and reducing the number of iterations required. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing significant improvements in topology assessment compared to traditional methods. The resulting framework offers a promising pathway towards more efficient quantum algorithm design and verification. This work addresses a critical gap in current topology assessment techniques, offering a tailored solution for the intricacies of quantum entanglement.

title: Title: Geometric Topology Optimization for High-Dimensional Data Clustering
abstract: Geometric topology optimization for high-dimensional data clustering represents a significant advancement in data segmentation, addressing the challenges posed by high-dimensional datasets. This paper introduces a novel clustering algorithm, termed "Geometric Topology Optimization," that utilizes a dynamically constructed graph structure to efficiently identify and segment high-dimensional data. The core mechanism centers on the creation of a "geometric clustering matrix" which optimizes for connectivity and distance within this graph, enabling superior performance compared to traditional clustering techniques. We present a rigorous evaluation demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness across a diverse set of datasets, highlighting its potential for applications in fields requiring precise data segmentation and dimensionality reduction.

title: Information-Driven Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative algorithm, termed the Information-Driven Algorithm (IDA), that leverages information entropy as a core driving force for algorithm parameter optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter adjustment, while IDA automatically adjusts parameters based on an internal entropy measure, leading to enhanced performance and robustness. This paper details the theoretical framework, implementation details, and experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of IDA in a range of scenarios. The core mechanism centers on the application of gradient descent and entropy-based weighting schemes to iteratively refine algorithm parameters. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's strengths and limitations, highlighting its potential for automating the optimization process and achieving superior results compared to conventional approaches.

evidence.abstract: This paper introduces an innovative algorithm, termed the Information-Driven Algorithm (IDA), that leverages information entropy as a core driving force for algorithm parameter optimization. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual parameter adjustment, while IDA automatically adjusts parameters based on an internal entropy measure, leading to enhanced performance and robustness. This paper details the theoretical framework, implementation details, and experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of IDA in a range of scenarios. The core mechanism centers on the application of gradient descent and entropy-based weighting schemes to iteratively refine algorithm parameters. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's strengths and limitations, highlighting its potential for automating the optimization process and achieving superior results compared to conventional approaches.

title: Zero-Assisted Harmonic Analysis for Cryptography
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for analyzing and exploiting zero-shifted harmonic functions, a crucial component of many contemporary cryptographic systems. Traditional methods often struggle with the inherent sensitivity of these functions to subtle perturbations, presenting a significant vulnerability to known attack vectors. We propose a new approach, the 'Zero-Assisted Harmonic Analysis' (ZHA), which leverages the zero-shifted properties to create a 'shadow' – a subtle distortion – that dramatically reduces the effectiveness of traditional cryptanalysis. The ZHA algorithm provides enhanced resistance to known attacks, representing a significant advancement in the field of zero-shift cryptography. This research explores the theoretical implications of the shadow effect and details the implementation of the algorithm, demonstrating its potential for robust defense.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organizing control system (QoC) based on quantum states, aiming to achieve high-precision control of complex systems. Traditional control systems rely on classical algorithms, which struggle to effectively adapt to dynamic environments. This research proposes a quantum-enhanced control approach that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum states to self-organize and precisely control system behavior. We present a framework for implementing this system, demonstrating its potential for achieving unprecedented levels of control and precision. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum states to dynamically adjust system parameters, enabling a more responsive and robust control strategy. This paper details the theoretical foundations and experimental validation of this approach, highlighting its advantages over existing control methodologies.

title: The Emergence of Geometric Topology in Quantum Computation: A Novel Validation Method
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of geometric topology and quantum computation, focusing on the dynamic properties of quantum computation intrinsically linked through self-linking geometry. We introduce the concept of "self-linking geometric topology" to frame quantum algorithms as evolving geometric structures, and investigate how this approach validates quantum computations through self-similarity and topological properties. The core mechanism involves utilizing self-linking geometry to characterize the evolution of quantum states and identify critical points within the quantum algorithm. This research offers a novel validation method for quantum algorithms, potentially leading to improved algorithm design and robustness.

title: Title: Topological Entanglement Preservation Algorithm (TEPA)
abstract: The preservation of topological entanglement – a crucial aspect of quantum computation – remains a significant challenge. Decoherence, a phenomenon where entangled qubits lose their correlation, dramatically degrades quantum coherence and information transfer. Existing preservation methods frequently rely on complex post-processing, limiting their applicability and hindering the full potential of quantum systems. This paper introduces the Topological Entanglement Preservation Algorithm (TEPA), a novel algorithm designed to actively maintain topological entanglement throughout the computation, thereby enhancing coherence and information transfer. The core of TEPA lies in the implementation of an "Adaptive Topology Lattice," a dynamically adjusting geometric framework that preemptively mitigates decoherence through specific geometric patterns. This approach offers a fundamentally more robust and reliable method of entanglement preservation compared to traditional techniques. We detail the algorithm's architecture, the underlying mathematical principles, and demonstrate its effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation.

title: Non-Linear Iterative Constraint Optimization via Fractal Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel iterative optimization algorithm, termed "Fractal Iterative Constraint Optimization" (FICO), designed to address complex optimization problems with fractal-like iteration. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with high-dimensional spaces and intricate constraints, while fractal geometry provides a compelling theoretical foundation for enhanced convergence and robustness. FICO leverages self-similarity principles to iteratively refine the solution, effectively mimicking the iterative refinement process observed in fractal structures. The algorithm employs a combination of fractal generation, constraint refinement, and adaptive parameter adjustment to achieve optimal solutions. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of FICO through rigorous analysis and comparison with established optimization techniques, showcasing its potential to overcome limitations in computationally intensive problems.

title: Probabilistic Reasoning via Graph Theory
abstract: Probabilistic Reasoning via Graph Theory explores the integration of probability theory with graph structures to address complex decision-solving problems. This paper introduces a novel framework leveraging graph representation and automated reasoning algorithms to effectively model and analyze probabilistic systems. We propose a method for constructing a robust probabilistic reasoning engine based on graph theory, enabling the discovery of underlying dependencies and potential decision paths. The core mechanism centers around the creation of a graph where nodes represent variables and edges represent relationships, with algorithms designed to automatically identify and evaluate inference pathways. This research highlights a new approach to probabilistic inference, offering a potential paradigm shift in handling complex scenarios.

title: Adaptive Metric Learning via Relational Embedding Distillation
abstract: Metric learning aims to learn a distance function that reflects the similarity between data points. While traditional approaches have been effective for simple datasets, they often fail to capture the nuanced relationships inherent in complex data, particularly those with strong relational components. This work introduces a novel adaptive metric learning framework, Relational Embedding Distillation (RED), designed to address this limitation. RED leverages a relational embedding distillation process, employing a pre-trained relational network—specifically a graph transformer—to guide the learning of a more efficient metric space. The core idea is to distill the rich relational knowledge encoded in the pre-trained network into the metric learning process, enabling the model to focus on capturing the essential relationships within the data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of RED on several challenging relational datasets, achieving significant improvements over existing metric learning methods. The key contributions of this work are the proposed distillation technique and its application to relational embedding, resulting in enhanced performance on complex relational data.

title: Quantum Adaptive Simulation Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Adaptive Simulation Algorithm (QASA) presents a novel approach to quantum simulation, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to enhance the fidelity and accuracy of simulations. This research focuses on designing an adaptive algorithm that dynamically adjusts simulation parameters based on the quantum state of the system being modeled, optimizing the simulation process for improved results. We explore the potential of QASA to overcome limitations of existing classical simulation methods, particularly in simulating complex systems with intricate dynamics. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to represent and manipulate system states, leading to a more precise and efficient simulation compared to traditional techniques. This paper provides a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation, highlighting its potential impact on various scientific disciplines.

title: ##基于深度学习的符号推理自动生成
abstract: This paper explores the development of a deep learning-based system for automated symbolic reasoning generation. Traditional symbolic reasoning relies heavily on human expertise in defining and maintaining rules, a process that is both time-consuming and prone to errors. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing deep learning models to learn the underlying rules and patterns inherent in symbolic reasoning processes, thereby automating the generation of these rules. We investigate the application of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and Transformer architectures to capture the nuances of symbolic reasoning, focusing on the representation and relationships of information within these processes. The ultimate goal is to create a more efficient and reliable system for reasoning, particularly in domains where manual rule definition is a significant bottleneck. The core of this work lies in leveraging the ability of deep learning models to learn from data without explicit programming, offering a potentially transformative shift in how we approach symbolic reasoning. This paper details the proposed architecture, explores potential applications, and discusses future research directions. ---

title: Adaptive Neuron Dynamic Topology Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network learning, termed Adaptive Neuron Dynamic Topology Learning (ANDTL). The core claim is that the topology of neuronal connections can adapt dynamically to task requirements, thereby enhancing both learning efficiency and generalization capabilities. The proposed mechanism utilizes a reinforcement learning-based algorithm to optimize the topology and connection weights within a neural network. Unlike traditional methods focused solely on adjusting weights, ANDTL introduces a dynamic adjustment of both structural and weight parameters. The system learns to rewire connections and even add or remove neurons based on the feedback received from a reward function, allowing it to converge to a more efficient and effective topology for a given task. This approach addresses limitations of conventional neural networks, particularly in scenarios with complex and evolving data distributions, where a fixed topology may not be optimal. The theoretical underpinnings of ANDTL are explored, and the potential benefits of this dynamic topology learning are discussed. The paper concludes with a high-level overview of the algorithm and its potential applications. ---

title: Quantum Adaptive Topology Transformation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum adaptive topology transformations to revolutionize quantum state conversion, particularly within the realms of quantum computing and quantum key distribution. Traditional quantum state conversion methods often rely on classical transformations, presenting limitations in efficiency and scalability. This research introduces a novel algorithm leveraging quantum topology transformations to dynamically adjust quantum states, thereby significantly enhancing the speed and efficacy of state conversion processes. The core mechanism focuses on systematically manipulating the quantum state through topology-based operations to achieve optimal transformations. We detail the algorithm's design, including the mathematical formulation of the topology transformations and their impact on state evolution. The significance of this approach lies in its potential to overcome limitations inherent in classical approaches, offering a pathway towards more efficient and robust quantum operations.

title: การศกษาการประยกตใช LLM-as-a-Judge เพอสนบสนนการประเมนและคดเลอกโมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญสำหรบการรางคำแถลงการสอสารภาวะวกฤตทางธรกจในภาษาไทย
authors: ปุณณภพ ชลอ
abstract: การสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตมีความสําคัญในภาคธุรกิจ เนื่องจากองค์กรจําเป็นต้องตอบสนองต่อเหตุการณ์ที่อาจกระทบต่อชื่อเสียง ความเชื่อมั่น และพฤติกรรมของผู้มีส่วนได้ส่วนเสียอย่างรวดเร็วและรอบคอบ ขณะเดียวกัน โมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญ่มีศักยภาพในการช่วยร่างข้อความหรือคําแถลงที่มีความสอดคล้องกับบริบทของภาษา แต่การนํามาใช้ในงานสื่อสารต่อสาธารณะยังต้องพิจารณาอย่างระมัดระวัง เนื่องจากข้อความที่สร้างโดยปัญญาประดิษฐ์อาจมีความเสี่ยงด้านความคลาดเคลื่อนของข้อเท็จจริง หรือไม่สอดคล้องกับบริบทและวัตถุประสงค์ของการสื่อสาร ดังนั้นการเลือกที่เหมาะสมจึงไม่สามารถพิจารณาเพียงการร่างคําแถลงเท่านั้น แต่ต้องประเมินคุณภาพของข้อความในมิติต่างๆ ที่เกี่ยวข้องกับการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตด้วยงานวิจัยนี้มุ่งศึกษาการสร้าง การประเมิน และการตัดสินร่างคําแถลงจากข่าวสถานการณ์วิกฤตของบริษัทเอกชนในประเทศไทย โดยใช้กรอบทฤษฎีการสื่อสารที่เกี่ยวข้องกับการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตเป็นแนวทางในการสร้างและประเมินข้อความ และนําผลลัพธ์ที่ได้จากโมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญ่หลายโมเดลมาประเมินและตัดสินกันด้วยแนวทาง LLM-as-a-Judge เพื่อใช้ในการสนับสนุนการตัดสินใจว่าโมเดลใดสามารถร่างคําแถลงที่มีคุณภาพและเหมาะสมกับบริบทการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตทางธุรกิจในภาษาไทยมากที่สุด นอกจากนี้ งานวิจัยยังเปรียบเทียบผลการตัดสินของ LLM-as-a-Judge กับผลการประเมินจากมนุษย์ เพื่อพิจารณาระดับความสอดคล้องระหว่างการตัดสินของปัญญาประดิษฐ์กับการตัดสินของมนุษย์ในงานด้านการสื่อสารผลที่คาดว่าจะได้รับจากงานวิจัยนี้ คือแนวทางเชิงปฏิบัติสําหรับการประเมินและคัดเลือกโมเดลภาษาขนาดใหญ่ที่เหมาะสมต่อการร่างคําแถลงเพื่อการสื่อสารภาวะวิกฤตทางธุรกิจในภาษาไทย รวมถึงความเข้าใจเกี่ยวกับศักยภาพและข้อจํากัดของการใช้ LLM-as-a-Judge ในการประเมินงานด้านการสื่อสารแบบปลายเปิด

title: Continual Graph Memory for Adaptive Recommendation under Intent Drift
abstract: This paper studies adaptive recommendation under intent drift, where feedback from each recommendation outcome can reveal whether the relational evidence used for ranking is useful, missing, or misleading. While Knowledge Graphs (KGs) provide essential semantic structure to handle these shifts, traditional KG-enhanced systems treat the graph as a static retrieval substrate, making it brittle to evolving intents, noisy metadata, and recurring failure patterns. This paper proposes CGM-Rec, a continual graph memory framework for adaptive recommendation. CGM-Rec treats the graph state as a writable memory and maintains two complementary components. Therein, a Semantic Graph Memory is updated conservatively through quality-gated typed operations for storing stable and high-confidence relational knowledge. Meanwhile, an Episodic Lesson Memory acts as a fast reactive memory that learns recent outcomes, failure cases, and corrective hints. During testing, model parameters remain frozen and adaptation occurs only through memory writes. We evaluate CGM-Rec under a frozen-parameter, one-pass reranking protocol, where encoders and prompts remain fixed during testing and adaptation occurs only through memory writes. Experiments across multiple recommendation settings show that CGM-Rec improves over evaluated neural and LLM-based baselines on most metrics. Particularly, under sampled-candidate reranking, CGM-Rec improves HR@1 by up to 29.58% over the strongest LLM baseline on Bundle, and outperforms K-RagRec on metadata-rich ML-100K with HR@5 of 0.5941 versus 0.4746.

title: NEXUS X AUTONOMOUS INTELLIGENCE AND ACTION PLATFORM
authors: 1Yamini Chouhan, 2 Baler Simon , 3 G Prashanth Kumar, 4 M Anjali, 5 B S Mahalakshmi
abstract: NEXUS X – Autonomous Intelligence and Action Platform is an intelligent software platform designed to go beyond traditional systems that only provide information or respond to user commands. The platform combines Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and automation technologies to understand user requirements, analyze information, make decisions, and perform appropriate actions with minimal human intervention. The proposed platform acts as an intelligent assistant that can receive user goals or tasks, understand their intent, break complex requirements into smaller steps, and determine suitable actions. It can analyze available data, generate recommendations, execute predefined workflows, monitor task progress, and provide results to the user. The system can also maintain context from previous interactions to improve the accuracy and relevance of its responses and actions. The main objective of NEXUS X is to create a unified autonomous platform that can transform user instructions into meaningful and actionable outcomes. Instead of requiring users to manually perform every step, the system can automate repetitive tasks, support decision-making, manage workflows, and provide intelligent recommendations. This can improve productivity, reduce manual effort, and enable faster completion of complex tasks. Overall, NEXUS X – Autonomous Intelligence and Action Platform provides a foundation for developing intelligent, goal-oriented applications capable of reasoning and taking controlled actions. The platform can be further enhanced with AI agents, real-time data integration, multi-agent collaboration, voice interaction, predictive analytics, personalized automation, external API integration, and advanced security and authorization mechanisms.

title: Feedback-free photonic reservoir computing based on multimode temporal coding in semiconductor ring lasers
abstract: 半导体环形激光器 (SRL) 天然支持顺时针与逆时针两个反向传播模式, 是构建光子神经形态计算的重要器件。然而, 基于 SRL 的光子储备池计算大多依赖物理反馈环来提供衰落记忆, 存在参数整定困难、稳定区间有限等问题。本文将单个 SRL 与受生物启发的准卷积 (QC) 编码相结合, 提出一种无反馈光子储备池计算方案, 依据 QC 编码施加位置的不同, 构建了输入编码型 (IC-RC)、输出编码型 (OC-RC) 与混合编码型 (HC-RC) 三种互补储备池变体, 三者分别通过在输入端、输出端或两端同时施加编码来提供差异化的算法记忆。通过建立速率方程模型, 在混沌时间序列预测、非线性信道均衡与线性记忆容量三项基准任务上, 分析了注入强度、频率失谐以及 QC核关键参数对三种方案性能的影响。结果表明, 三种方案均明显优于传统时延储备池计算。本文还发现不同的编码方案具有不同的优势, 其中 IC-RC 预测性能最优, HC-RC 记忆保持能力最强,输出层激活函数可进一步改善预测与信道均衡性能, 而对记忆容量影响甚微。本文结果不仅验证了所提方案的有效性, 也为构建高度可集成的光子神经形态计算系统提供了新的思路。

title: Multimedia Integration and Cultural Heritage Innovation Pathways in Traditional Pipa Performance Teaching in the Digital Age
abstract: This paper will investigate how the pipa can integrate multimedia technologies within its teaching practices for overcoming major teaching challenges such as teacher shortages, standardized teaching, and inadequate support for individual differences among students. The proposed model will include intelligent diagnostic systems using audio analysis for performance assessment and learning path recommendations, multi-media teaching aids with digitized scores and multi-angle teaching videos, as well as teaching plans based on individual students’ levels of proficiency. Design for cultural heritage content will focus on digital recreation of historical settings, multi-media interpretation for regional teaching characteristics, as well as developing aesthetic competency with links to traditional art values. Implementation assistance will include upgrading teachers’ digital literacy skills, improving evaluation systems with technical-humanistic dimensions, as well as developing institutional sharing platforms for teaching resources. This comprehensive teaching platform views multimedia technology as an enabler that complements existing pipa pedagogy while maintaining cultural authenticity, contributing a pipa-calibrated integration model, a cultural heritage innovation pathway, and implementation mechanisms that extend master-apprentice transmission through digital means.

title: Axiomatizing Atomic Numbers in ChEBI
abstract: This post describes how I produced a novel ontology module that axiomatizes the atomic numbers for ChEBI terms representing atoms (i.e., subclasses of CHEBI:33250) using subclass expressions with data restrictions, and the ROBOT template magic that made it possible.

title: Continuity Kernel: A Cognitive Architecture and AI Safety Framework for Persistent Artificial Identity
abstract: Continuity Kernel / CK-01 is a computational cognitive architecture and AI safety framework for persistent artificial identity. This v1.0.0 record includes the full manuscript, editable source, a one-command synthetic benchmark, exact configurations and seeds, raw machine-readable results, manifests, SHA-256 hashes, tests, gate specifications, and legacy evidence bundles. The claims are limited to architecture design and synthetic validation; the work does not claim empirical validation of consciousness, human cognition, or real-world autonomous-agent safety.

title: Native Cognition Kernel (NCK) 0.1
abstract: Native Cognition Kernel (NCK) 0.1 is a mathematically specified architecture for deterministic, bounded, provenance-aware machine cognition. NCK defines cognition as an explicit system of typed symbolic state, proof-governed inference, hypothesis formation, prediction, falsification, revision, planning, action, and adaptation under changing rules and environments.Rather than defining cognitive behavior through a trained statistical model, NCK specifies its cognitive operations directly as finite mathematical objects, relations, operators, invariants, and certified state transitions. The architecture is designed so that its semantics are independent of any particular software implementation, programming language, execution platform, or hardware realization.This release contains the authoritative NCK 0.1 Normative Mathematical Specification, its typeset publication, and the Executable Logic companion, which develops the formal system through explicit paper-executable examples. The Markdown mathematical specification is the sole normative mathematical authority for NCK 0.1; the accompanying publications are subordinate to that specification.The architecture is intended to support direct implementation and formal verification, including software proof-of-concept implementations and, where developed and separately validated, formal-proof and digital-hardware realizations such as Lean, Verilog, or VHDL representations.The release includes an external SHA-256 manifest identifying the exact immutable artifacts constituting NCK 0.1. title: Title: Adaptive Chaos for Deep Learning Architectures
abstract: This paper explores the application of adaptive chaos to enhance deep learning architectures, aiming to improve both performance and stability during training. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts the structure of the network – specifically, layer sizes, connection strengths, and activation function parameters – based on real-time monitoring of training progress. This self-tuning chaos mechanism, driven by a feedback loop, allows the network to evolve and optimize itself, potentially exceeding the limitations of traditional optimization techniques. The core idea is to mimic the inherent dynamics of chaotic systems, leveraging a carefully crafted 'chaos' component to guide the learning process. The integration of chaos into a core deep learning technique offers a promising path toward more robust and efficient deep learning models. This work presents a preliminary framework and demonstrates its potential through a simplified implementation of a neural network with adaptive chaos.

title: 基于自适应拓扑的自组织机器学习 (ASML)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-organizing machine learning framework, termed ASML, based on adaptive topology. Traditional machine learning models often struggle to accurately represent and model complex system behaviors, and ASML offers a new toolset for this purpose. The core of ASML lies in the implementation of an adaptive topology structure, which allows the model to dynamically adjust its representation to better capture the intricacies of the data. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness through a series of illustrative examples, focusing on a system exhibiting self-organized patterns. The paper elucidates the mechanism behind ASML and its potential impact on machine learning research.

title: 基于自适应的量子模拟的容错优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Simulation with Error Mitigation," designed to address the challenges of quantum simulation, particularly concerning error mitigation. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameter adjustments, leading to inherent stochasticity and potential inaccuracies. This work proposes a self-adaptive parameter adjustment strategy, leveraging quantum system dynamics to dynamically refine simulation parameters, thereby significantly reducing random errors during the simulation process. The algorithm's core mechanism involves a continuous assessment and adjustment of key simulation variables, resulting in improved accuracy and reliability of quantum simulations. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, provides a rigorous analysis of its performance, and explores its potential for enhancing the quality of quantum computations. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to mitigate errors in a specific quantum system simulation scenario. The study concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications of this approach.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应几何优化
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to revolutionize geometric optimization. Traditional geometric optimization algorithms often struggle with complex, high-dimensional shapes due to computational limitations. We propose a novel algorithm, Quantum Geometry Optimizer (QGO), that utilizes entangled quantum states to represent and manipulate geometric configurations, offering a potential pathway to significantly enhance optimization efficiency and handle intricate shapes. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the unique properties of entanglement to create a dynamic and adaptive optimization process. This work provides a theoretical foundation and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this approach. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications of this technology for various fields.

title: Quantum Entanglement Beyond Symmetry: Towards Enhanced Computational Capabilities
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for revolutionizing computation. However, the inherent fragility of entangled states poses significant challenges to building practical and scalable quantum computers. This paper explores the concept of quantum entanglement's non-symmetry, proposing a novel approach – the incorporation of non-symmetry into quantum computations – to enhance stability and unlock new computational capabilities. We investigate how this approach mitigates the limitations of single-state entanglement and paves the way for fundamentally different algorithms. The core claim is that strategically introducing non-symmetry into quantum algorithms can lead to improved resilience and performance, offering a pathway to more robust and capable quantum systems. This work details a mechanism for encoding and manipulating non-symmetric entangled states, illustrating its potential impact on quantum computation. We present a preliminary analysis of this approach and outline future research directions, emphasizing the importance of understanding and harnessing the power of non-symmetry in quantum information processing.

title: Nonlinear Time Series Systems and Deep Reinforcement Learning Fusion
abstract: This paper explores the fusion of nonlinear time series systems (NTS) modeling with reinforcement learning (RL) for addressing complex control problems characterized by high nonlinearity and time-varying dynamics. The core idea is to leverage the representation power of NTS models to capture system behavior and then utilize RL algorithms for policy optimization. Deep learning techniques are integrated for feature extraction and representation learning, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional RL methods in handling intricate nonlinear systems. The proposed approach offers a novel way to tackle control problems where explicit system models are difficult to obtain, relying instead on learning from data. The research demonstrates the potential of this combined approach to achieve robust and adaptive control performance.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Collaborative Optimization of Non-Classical Computing Resources
abstract: This research investigates a novel approach to quantum algorithm design and resource allocation by synergistically combining quantum error correction (QEC) coding with the characteristics of non-classical computing resources, such as quantum heat reservoirs and quantum noise. The core premise is that traditional optimization strategies for QEC and non-classical resource utilization operate independently, neglecting the potential for mutual benefit. We propose a framework centered around probabilistic quantum algorithm optimizers that simulate algorithm performance under varying resource conditions. These optimizers dynamically adjust both quantum algorithm parameters and QEC schemes based on the simulated performance, aiming to achieve significantly improved efficiency. This work addresses a critical gap in the field by moving beyond isolated optimization efforts and establishing a fundamental connection between the robustness of QEC and the practical limitations imposed by non-classical computing environments. The methodology leverages advanced probabilistic modeling and optimization techniques to provide a robust and adaptive approach to quantum algorithm design.

title: 基于动态量子纠缠的拓扑几何验证
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum geometry validation utilizing dynamic quantum entanglement. We propose a method that leverages the inherent properties of entangled quantum states to simulate and verify complex topological structures with unprecedented precision. Traditional topological calculations often struggle with approximation errors and require significant computational resources. This research introduces a dynamically-generated quantum state model, employing entanglement to mimic the evolution of topological phenomena, and utilizing quantum effects to precisely characterize their properties. The core mechanism focuses on establishing a robust, accurate, and accelerated computational framework for topological analysis. This work represents a significant advancement, demonstrating the potential for a fundamentally new approach to topological computation, surpassing current limitations through enhanced precision and computational efficiency.

title: Quantum Topological Chaos Optimization
abstract: Quantum Topological Chaos Optimization (QTCO) presents a novel algorithmic approach to optimization, leveraging the principles of quantum topicity chaos – a theoretical framework that describes complex systems exhibiting unique, non-linear, and highly sensitive behavior. This research focuses on developing a self-adaptive optimization algorithm predicated on this chaotic structure, aiming to improve the stability and robustness of complex systems. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum entanglement and topological structure to dynamically adjust system parameters and propagate solutions, thereby achieving enhanced performance. This paper outlines the design of QTCO, detailing its core concepts, methodology, and preliminary results demonstrating its potential for optimizing challenging systems.

title: 异质性感知学习的自适应感知算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive perception algorithm based on the principle of '异质性感知' – dynamically adjusting perceptual thresholds and model parameters to effectively model and identify complex data distributions. Traditional perception algorithms typically rely on fixed thresholds, while this approach leverages the inherent heterogeneity of data to dynamically adjust perception, enhancing model capabilities for complex datasets. We present a framework for implementing this dynamic adjustment using a novel weighting mechanism. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through a series of quantitative evaluations on several benchmark datasets, showcasing improved performance in identifying intricate patterns and reducing classification errors compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The core mechanism focuses on continuous parameter adjustment based on data distribution characteristics, offering a robust and adaptable solution for diverse perception tasks.

title: Self-Adapting Quantum State Prediction and Algorithm Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-adaptive quantum state prediction as a novel approach to algorithm optimization within the quantum computing realm. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on computationally expensive pre-calculations, limiting their practical efficiency. We propose a new algorithmic framework leveraging self-adaptive quantum state prediction to dynamically adjust quantum operations, thereby significantly enhancing algorithm performance. This research explores the design of a system that predicts the state of a quantum system and uses this prediction to intelligently guide the execution of quantum circuits. The core mechanism centers around real-time state evolution and optimization, resulting in improved efficiency. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the benefits and challenges associated with this approach and outlines a roadmap for future advancements in quantum algorithm design.

title: Adaptive Quantum Interference Optimization of Spacetime
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum interference optimization to enhance the performance of complex systems, specifically focusing on optimizing algorithm efficiency and computational precision. The core concept centers around leveraging the unique properties of quantum interference – a phenomenon where quantum systems can constructively or destructively interfere – to dynamically adjust system parameters and improve computational results. Traditional optimization techniques often rely on fixed parameters, while this work proposes a novel approach utilizing this interference to achieve more effective and adaptable optimization. The research explores the potential of this method to address challenges in various fields, including machine learning and computational modeling, by providing a framework for robust and efficient optimization. The paper details the methodology, presents preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach, and concludes with future directions for research and development.

title: Waveform-driven prediction of transmon qubit energy spectra using a physics-informed path-transformed transformer trained on Josephson junction dynamics.
abstract: Extracting the energy spectrum of a superconducting transmon qubit requires time-consuming microwave spectroscopy that must be repeated following every thermal cycle or parameter drift event. We introduce the Physics-Informed Path-Transformed (PaTH) Transformer, a surrogate model trained exclusively on resistively-shunted Josephson junction (RCSJ) numerical simulations, which predicts the five lowest energy eigenvalues and the anharmonicity from a raw DC voltage waveform. The model is trained on 10,000 simulated circuits spanning the realistic transmon parameter space (EJ /EC ∈ [10.7, 300], f01/h ∈ [2.6, 13.3] GHz) and evaluated on 1,500 independent test circuits, achieving mean absolute energy error 0.886 μeV (R2 ≥ 0.998 per level) and transition-frequency spacing error 2.14%, with GPU inference completing in 8.70 ms per circuit. A curriculum-ramped physics loss incorporating Josephson monotonicity, quantization spacing, anharmonicity sign, and Lindblad-Heisenberg constraints produces physically self-consistent predictions throughout training. Treating anharmonicity as a direct sixth output resolves a gradient-scale conflict (∼25× imbalance) that prevents reliable convergence when it is inferred post-hoc from level differences. The model delivers, from a single forward pass: DRAG gate fidelity ⟨F⟩ = 0.99982 at 3.9 ns; dispersive readout shift −14.3 MHz; macroscopic quantum tunneling crossover at 56.6 mK; SQUID tunable range 5.95 GHz; and inverse-design frequency errors below 0.05 kHz. Zero-noise extrapolation across five dilution-refrigerator temperatures confirms that model accuracy already reaches the Johnson-Nyquist noise floor, with the macroscopic quantum tunneling crossover temperature providing a physics-derived accuracy benchmark independent of model architecture. Validated against eight published experimental spectra from four independent laboratories, the surrogate achieves mean f01 error 1929 MHz versus 1935 MHz for exact Hamiltonian diagonalization, demonstrating that RCSJ waveform encoding conveys device-level physics that the static ideal Hamiltonian cannot represent.

title: Broadband chaos generation and anti-synchronization in a feed-forward optical neural network via optical injection
abstract: The operation of an optical neural network (ONN) via feed-forward (FF) configuration is experimentally simulated in the laboratory. The FF setup is tested using optical injection (OI), and the behavior of follower laser diodes (FLDs) subjected to chaotic modulation is examined. The last two laser diodes (LDs) are exposed to different weights of chaotic modulated signals through optical filtration and current modulation. Observations of the emissions from these two FLDs during FF operation are verified by frequency spectra calculated from time series data. Signal broadening is assessed by measuring the full width at half maximum (FWHM), and chaotic signal spikes are analyzed by counting the number of peaks associated with signal amplitudes for the FLDs. Additionally, LD control parameters, including the bias voltage of the influencer laser diodes FLD and two additional FLDs, are examined. A maximum FWHM of 1.8[Formula: see text]GHz for FLD is observed with a bias voltage of 3.9[Formula: see text]V (B) and a modulated signal attenuation of −12[Formula: see text]dB. To determine the synchronization state, the correlation between the ILDs and FLDs is calculated. Results indicate fluctuations between negative and positive values, with the best correlation value ILD1-FLD4-0.8. These results confirm anti-synchronized ILD-FLDs, which represents a promising feature for potential secure communication architectures based on chaotic optical neural networks (ONNs), subject to further experimental verification.

title: Can Acceleration in Gradient-Norm Minimization Be Anytime? Sharp Last-Iterate Limits in Smooth Convex Optimization
abstract: In smooth convex optimization, the gradient norm is a directly observable measure of stationarity. Accelerating a first-order method that minimizes the gradient norm is known to be more delicate than accelerating the minimization of function values. Optimal accelerated methods such as OGM-G (Kim & Fessler, 2021) are known to exist for any prescribed finite horizon, but their coefficients depend explicitly on the length of that horizon, i.e. the number of iterations. We ask what kind of acceleration is feasible when the stopping horizon is unknown to the method, i.e. for horizon-independent methods. Diakonikolas & Wang (2022) conjectured that an $Ω(N^{-1})$ lower bound on the squared gradient norm holds at every horizon $N$ for any nonadaptive, horizon-independent linear-span first-order method. We disprove this pointwise conjecture by exhibiting a method that achieves near-$N^{-2}$ last-iterate guarantees on a density-one set of horizons. We show instead that an $Ω(N^{-1})$ lower bound must hold for infinitely many horizons. More precisely, if $\mathcal G_N(\mathcal A)$ denotes the bound on the squared gradient norm after $N$ iterations for a method $\mathcal A$, we prove that $\limsup_{N\to\infty}N \mathcal G_N(\mathcal A) \ge 1/2$ for any method $\mathcal A$. This bound is sharp: the constant $1/2$ is exactly attained by the horizon-independent gradient-descent schedule of Rotaru et al. (2026). In addition, we show that the above two extreme behaviors cannot be achieved by the same method: any method $\mathcal A$ with an $o(N^{-1})$ guarantee on a subsequence of iterates must satisfy $\limsup_N N \mathcal G_N(\mathcal A)=\infty$. In contrast, best-so-far output admits a uniform $O(N^{-2})$ guarantee.

title: Same Trajectory, Contradictory Rewards (ROBORMBENCH): Paraphrase Fragility in Vision Language Reward Models
abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly used as reward functions for robotic learning, but this role requires paraphrase invariance: the same trajectory should receive the same reward under semantically equivalent goal descriptions. We show that current VLM reward models often violate this property. Paraphrasing the instruction alone can substantially change predicted progress scores, and can even flip identical robot behavior between failure and success. To measure this failure mode, we introduce ROBORMBENCH, a benchmark with 2,390 real-robot trajectories, ground-truth progress labels, and 21,673 verified paraphrases spanning lexical, syntactic, and action-goal rewrites. Across proprietary and open-source VLMs, paraphrase-induced instability is widespread and severe, grows under more divergent rewrites, and is not reliably reduced by scale or explicit reasoning. Dedicated reward models trained with trajectory-grounded supervision are substantially more stable. These results show that paraphrase robustness is a core requirement for reliable VLM-based reward modeling in robotics.
