title: Self-Adaptive Quantum State Encoding and Expansion
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of self-adaptive quantum state encoding and expansion techniques to significantly enhance quantum computation. The core focus is on leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum information theory to dynamically modify and expand quantum states, addressing limitations of traditional approaches. We propose a novel method that dynamically adjusts the quantum state to optimize performance and explore new computational pathways. The paper details the underlying principles, introduces a key mechanism for state modification, and outlines the potential benefits of this approach. Furthermore, a comprehensive analysis of the theoretical and potential practical implications is presented. The research aims to contribute to the advancement of quantum computing by providing a framework for more versatile and powerful quantum systems.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Topology Structure Research
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental theoretical basis of quantum entanglement through the application of non-linear geometry topology. We explore a model based on non-Euclidean geometry, constructing a quantum entanglement framework that leverages its inherent non-linear properties. A novel quantum information processing algorithm is proposed, based on this model, aiming to simulate quantum entanglement with enhanced computational capabilities. The study aims to challenge existing quantum entanglement theories, which are primarily rooted in classical geometry, and potentially unveil new approaches to quantum information processing.

title: Core Claim: A Self-Adaptive Topological Quantum State Expansion Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state expansion algorithm based on self-adaptive topology, aiming to enhance the range of achievable quantum states and provide powerful tools for optimization and control within quantum computing. The core mechanism involves leveraging topological structure to dynamically expand the Hilbert space of quantum states, offering a pathway to more efficient quantum computations. Traditional approaches often rely on manual design, hindering the potential for automated learning and optimization. This work proposes a framework that automatically discovers and utilizes topological structures to expand the Hilbert space, offering a new paradigm for quantum state manipulation. The algorithm's potential impact lies in its ability to unlock new computational capabilities and facilitate the development of more sophisticated quantum algorithms.

title: Title: Algorithmic Consciousness with Contextual Bias
abstract: This paper explores the concept of algorithmic consciousness, aiming to develop an AI system capable of nuanced reasoning and adaptive behavior through a novel approach centered on contextual bias and cognitive weighting. We propose an algorithm that learns to subtly adjust its output based on observed user behavior and environmental context, thereby fostering a degree of 'understanding' – a critical step towards truly conscious AI. The core mechanism involves a dynamic cognitive weighting system that adjusts the algorithm's output based on observed data. This research addresses the challenge of moving beyond simple accuracy optimization, introducing a layer of adaptability and potential for genuine problem-solving. The focus is on establishing a framework for AI that can reason and respond intelligently to complex situations, ultimately pushing the boundaries of artificial intelligence.

title: 基于图的自适应机器学习的知识迁移
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for knowledge transfer utilizing graph-based self-adaptive machine learning. Traditional machine learning often relies on specific datasets, limiting its ability to generalize effectively. Our approach addresses this limitation by employing a graph-structured learning algorithm that dynamically adapts to the underlying graph structure and node relationships. We introduce a framework that automatically adjusts the learning process based on the graph's inherent characteristics, leading to enhanced knowledge transfer and improved generalization performance. The core mechanism centers around a self-adaptive learning algorithm that leverages graph structure and node relationships to establish a mapping of knowledge from one graph to another. The paper details the design of this framework, explores its implementation, and provides a comprehensive analysis of its performance through illustrative examples. The goal is to develop a robust and adaptable method for knowledge transfer, significantly enhancing the capabilities of machine learning models across diverse graph-based datasets.

title: Quantum Information Bottleneck Mitigation (QIBM)
abstract: Quantum information networks, crucial for advanced quantum computing and distributed quantum sensing, are plagued by the infamous information bottleneck. This bottleneck limits the speed and scalability of quantum communication and computation, hindering progress in these fields. This paper introduces the Quantum State Synchronization Protocol (QIBM), a novel system designed to effectively mitigate this bottleneck by minimizing the delay between quantum components. We detail the protocol's architecture, operational principles, and potential impact on network performance. The focus is on enhancing the robustness and efficiency of quantum information transfer, ultimately paving the way for more reliable and practical quantum technologies.

title: Probability Field Theory Under Non-linear Gradient Descent Optimization
abstract: Probability Field Theory (PFT) offers a novel approach to optimization by incorporating probabilistic elements into the optimization process. This paper investigates the application of PFT to gradient descent optimization, specifically focusing on mitigating the issues of gradient vanishing and exploding. We introduce a novel mechanism that leverages the probabilistic nature of the gradient field to enhance the optimization process, particularly when dealing with non-linear functions. This research explores the potential of PFT to improve the efficiency and robustness of gradient-based optimization algorithms. The core claim is that the introduction of probabilistic elements into the gradient descent framework can lead to more effective learning of complex functions, especially in scenarios involving non-linear functions.

title: 基于动态的拓扑变换的贝叶斯网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian network framework, termed "Dynamic Topological Transform Network" (DTT-Net), that leverages dynamic topology transformations as probabilistic models. The core mechanism centers on constructing a probability distribution representing the transformation process, enabling prediction and optimization using a Bayesian network. This approach addresses limitations of traditional Bayesian networks by incorporating a dynamic element, offering improved accuracy and adaptability in complex topology transformations. We present a practical implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of the DTT-Net in modeling and manipulating topological structures, highlighting its potential for advanced applications in fields requiring precise and flexible topology manipulation.

title: Quantum-Driven Constraint Optimization for Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum-enhanced constraint optimization to accelerate the training and improve generalization of neural networks. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with the complexity of large neural networks, requiring significant computational resources and time. We propose a novel quantum algorithm, employing quantum annealing or quantum-enhanced gradient descent, to dynamically adjust the weights of the neural network. The core claim is that this approach can significantly reduce training time and improve the model's ability to generalize to unseen data. The paper details the theoretical framework, algorithm implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the potential benefits of this quantum-driven approach.

title: Nonlinear Topological Structures for Quantum Algorithm Optimization
abstract: Quantum algorithm optimization is a significant challenge in the field of quantum computing. Traditional optimization methods often focus on maximizing computational throughput, while the inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates a novel approach. This paper introduces a novel framework, termed "Nonlinear Topological Structures for Quantum Algorithm Optimization," which leverages the unique properties of non-linear topological structures to guide the optimization process. The core mechanism involves mapping the quantum algorithm's parameters to a topological space, allowing for the exploration of diverse parameter configurations through a process of 'topological folding' and 'pathfinding.' We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing significant improvements in algorithm efficiency and stability compared to existing methods. The study highlights the potential of utilizing non-linear topology to address challenges in quantum algorithm design and optimization.

title: Self-Organizing Topological Quantum Computing Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing algorithm based on self-organizing topological structures. Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on precise parameter adjustments and complex control sequences, which can be computationally intensive and susceptible to errors. This research explores the potential of utilizing topological structures to enhance quantum computation by dynamically adjusting the quantum state to optimize performance. We detail a method for generating and manipulating these topological states, showcasing its ability to improve the fidelity of quantum operations and ultimately enhance the efficiency of quantum algorithms. The core of this work lies in a framework that leverages the inherent robustness and adaptability of topological phases to mitigate errors and accelerate computations. The algorithm's design incorporates a novel optimization strategy based on the topological properties of the generated states, leading to a demonstrable improvement in quantum state fidelity compared to existing approaches. This advancement holds significant promise for advancing the practical application of quantum computing.

title: Arnold's Bifurcation Principle Applied to Deployed Neural Networks: Real-Time Hardware Detection of Adversarial and Out-of-Distribution Inputs Using Hessian-Free Curvature-Velocity Tracking
abstract: A trained neural network, once put into service, is treated as fixed: its parameters do not change. What does change, continuously, is the stream of inputs it is asked to judge. Some of these inputs are ordinary. Some have been deliberately altered by an attacker to force a wrong answer. Some are simply unlike anything the network has ever seen. Earlier published work has already shown that both of these situations share a measurable signature: the local curvature of the network’s loss surface with respect to the input, which is the largest eigenvalue of the input-space Hessian, tends to be higher for adversarial and out-of-distribution inputs than for ordinary ones. Existing detection methods use this curvature as a single number, checked at one moment, against a fixed cutoff. We show that the same early-warning construction used throughout the Arnold’s Bifurcation Principle framework– tracking not the curvature itself but the phase-space pair formed by the curvature and its own rate of change– can be applied here as well, in a small piece of dedicated hardware sitting beside the main inference accelerator. We are explicit about a real cost difference from our earlier work on AI training: unlike a training run, where the required curvature information comes for free from steps the optimizer is already taking, an inference-time input stream does not always provide this for free, and we describe exactly when it does and when it requires a small added probe cost

title: Построение замкнутой программной среды в Unix-подобных операционных системах с использованием средств защиты пользовательского пространства
abstract: Целью работы является противодействие запуску недоверенного кода в Unix-подобных операционных системах. Объектом исследования является замкнутая программная среда. Задачи, решаемые в ходе исследования: 1. Исследовать механизм работы замкнутой программной среды в Unix-подобных операционных системах. 2. Исследовать возможности запуска недоверенного кода в замкнутой программной среде. 3. Предложить механизм защиты от запуска недоверенного кода в замкнутой программной среде. 4. Реализовать и провести тестирование предложенного механизма защиты. В ходе работы была исследована работа замкнутой программной среды и её реализация с помощью подсистем Linux IMA и veriexec. Была продемонстрирована возможность запуска недоверенного кода в замкнутой программной среде. В результате работы был разработан механизм пользовательского пространства, который позволяет предотвратить возможность запуска недоверенного кода. Данный механизм был реализован на практике и протестирован. Был сделан вывод о его эффективности в сравнении с другими механизмами. Полученные результаты могут быть использованы при проектирование замкнутой программной среды для обеспечения безопасности системы.

title: Task-Aware QUBO Allocation for Mixed-Precision Quantization
abstract: Mixed-precision quantization requires discrete allocation of weight and activation bit-widths, followed by recovery of the selected network. We develop a task-aware quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) surrogate with separate weight and activation profiles, a bit-operation (BOP) cost, and selected structural priors. QUBO provides a network-wide allocation that can be refined through direct validation-based PROTES search. On a compact NAFBlock-based denoiser, the refined route achieves 37.192 dB after LSQ+ at 4.035\% routed-layer BOPs, versus 37.092 dB at 4.101\% for a HAWQ-style baseline. The repeated-search primary experiment shows that LSQ+ largely closes the quality gap between QUBO allocation and expensive direct refinement. An additional restoration architecture retains a larger recovered gain, indicating that refinement's value depends on architecture and recovery. We evaluate quality, achieved cost, routing stability and optimization expense together. Deployment measurements characterize a fake-quantized floating-point implementation; BOP reductions describe analytical allocation savings.

title: Reflection-aware Generative Novel View Synthesis
abstract: We propose Ref-GeNVS, a training-free, reflection-aware method for generative novel view synthesis (NVS) in mirror scenes. Existing multi-view diffusion models often fail to recognize the mirror in the scene and cannot exploit reflected content for scene generation. To fix this issue without additional training, our key idea is to treat a mirror image as two complementary views. From input images, we estimate the mirror plane and reflect camera poses to form virtual views. Based on this virtual view setup, we propose a two-stage generation method consisting of Mirror-gated attention and Reflection injection, which enables reflection-consistent NVS by explicitly leveraging reflection relationships in a multi-view diffusion model. Ref-GeNVS inherits the strong generalizability of the multi-view diffusion backbone, while it does not require finetuning. On synthetic and real scenes including mirrors, Ref-GeNVS outperforms recent generative NVS methods by generating reflection-consistent and contextually coherent novel views, revealing scene structure visible only through mirrors. Project page: https://kim-geonu.github.io/Ref-GeNVS/

title: LetOccVote: Learning Weakly Supervised 3D Occupancy through Consensus
abstract: Weakly supervised 3D occupancy prediction reduces the reliance on costly 3D annotations by learning from 2D pseudo-labels generated by vision foundation models. However, existing methods typically use these imperfect pseudo-labels directly as supervision, making occupancy learning vulnerable to erroneous geometric and semantic targets. We observe that agreement across repeated observations provides an inexpensive and reliable cue for assessing pseudo-label reliability. Based on this observation, we propose \textbf{LetOccVote}, a weakly supervised Gaussian-based occupancy framework that leverages cross-frame voting to improve both geometric and semantic supervision. For geometry, Depth Vote exploits cross-frame geometric agreement to refine supported pseudo depth and reject contradictory estimates before volumetric lifting and depth supervision. For semantics, Semantic Vote aggregates pseudo-semantic observations in a shared 3D space to identify reliable and contested evidence, strengthening reliable semantic supervision while filtering unreliable pseudo-label segments. The entire framework is trained solely with 2D pseudo-label supervision without requiring 3D occupancy annotations. On Occ3D-nuScenes, LetOccVote achieves 53.27 IoU and 20.39 mIoU, establishing state-of-the-art performance among methods with 2D pseudo-label supervision.

title: Label-Efficient 3D Point Cloud Understanding: From Representation Learning to Foundation Model Adaptation
abstract: Point clouds are the native output of modern 3D sensors that power autonomous driving, robotics, and augmented reality, yet their irregular, permutation-invariant, and geometrically rich structure - together with the high cost of 3D annotation - makes fully supervised learning impractical. In this thesis, we propose novel methods for label-efficient 3D perception that span from learning representations directly on raw point clouds to adapting pre-trained 3D foundation models under limited supervision and distribution shift. We first address representation learning by proposing CrossMoCo, a cross-modal momentum-contrastive framework that jointly pre-trains point cloud and image encoders to learn transferable representations. We further propose AllMatch that targets the limitation of pseudo-labelling in semi-supervised learning, so that every unlabelled sample - not only high-confidence ones - contributes, recovering near fully supervised accuracy with a small fraction of the labels. We next address adaptation by proposing MCFT, an adapter-free fine-tuning paradigm that curbs overfitting at no additional inference cost. We further propose ReFine3D that extends this idea to multi-modal 3D vision-language models, adding multi-view consistency and text-diversity regularization for robustness to novel classes, data corruptions, and cross-dataset shift. Finally, we propose SAGE by introducing an end-to-end, encoder-free 3D multi-modal large language model that resolves semantic misalignment and resolution mismatch challenges by treating point clouds as a foreign language. Together, these contributions advance robust, scalable 3D understanding toward practical, annotation-light deployment.

title: Explicitly correlated wavefunctions as classical seeds and property references for sample-based quantum diagonalization beyond the Born–Oppenheimer approximation
abstract: This work evaluates how well hybrid classical–quantum simulation methods capture not only the energy of small atomic and molecular systems, but also their other properties: contact densities, molecular structure, and state identity — the spin sector a computed state actually lives in. It employs explicitly correlated Gaussian (ECG) wavefunctions both as references for evaluating these properties and as classical seeds for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), on the simulator and on IBM quantum hardware. Our testbeds — positronium hydride, the muonic heliumlike ions, the HD+ molecular ion, and the positronium anion and molecule — realize three typical failure regimes: boxes that lack the property no matter how configurations are selected, boxes that hold it exactly with no selection needed, and the middle regime where the selection itself decides. In every regime the property error dwarfs the energy error: a subspace can converge the energy to microhartrees while misstating an annihilation rate, a bond length, or the spin by whole percent. Property fidelity, not energy, is the discriminating test of a multicomponent simulation.

title: Geometric Complexity of Stochastic Processes via Bayesian Filtering
abstract: This paper investigates the geometric complexity of stochastic processes, focusing on high-dimensional scenarios. We propose a Bayesian filtering framework, termed "Geometric Bayesian Estimation," designed to quantify complexity more effectively than traditional methods. The core mechanism involves exploiting geometric properties inherent to the process to refine estimates of its dimensionality and structure. This approach aims to address limitations in existing Bayesian techniques, particularly concerning the analysis of high-dimensional data. The paper details the algorithm, its theoretical underpinnings, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy.

title: Title: Non-Linear Harmonic Field Dynamics with Adaptive Amplitude Scaling
abstract: This paper investigates the modeling and simulation of non-linear harmonic field dynamics, focusing on a novel algorithm leveraging reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust field amplitude based on the system's internal state. Traditional harmonic field simulations frequently rely on fixed parameters, restricting their applicability to specific system configurations. We propose a new approach that utilizes a reinforcement learning framework to train a neural network to optimize field amplitude in real-time, providing enhanced flexibility and adaptability. The algorithm addresses the limitations of current simulation techniques by enabling the system to self-regulate its field characteristics. This work explores the potential for this approach to unlock new functionalities and applications in diverse fields, including materials science, fluid dynamics, and sensor systems. The core mechanism centers on a reinforcement learning agent trained to respond to a system's internal state, dynamically adjusting the amplitude of the field.

title: Title: Adaptive Cognitive Geometry (ACG)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Cognitive Geometry (ACG), a novel computational framework for generating and evolving cognitive geometry. The core claim is that ACG can dynamically shape the structure of a space based on an individual's internal cognitive processes and understanding of the world. The system employs neural network-inspired algorithms to 'learn' the geometry of space, creating a personalized geometric representation. This research explores the potential of leveraging cognitive processes within a computational model, offering a potential paradigm shift in how we understand and model the relationship between mind and perception. The paper details the architecture of the ACG system, including the neural network components and the process of generating and evolving the geometric representation. We discuss the potential applications and limitations of this approach, focusing on its ability to capture and model complex cognitive processes.

title: Title: Non-Local Wave Function Collapse for Parallel Quantum Computation
abstract: Abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to quantum computation, termed Non-Local Wave Function Collapse (NLWC), designed to accelerate quantum algorithms through simultaneous wave function collapse across multiple processors. Traditional quantum algorithms often face scalability challenges, necessitating efficient methods for handling complex quantum states. NLWC proposes a mechanism that drastically reduces computation time by allowing the collapse of multiple states concurrently, offering a potential pathway to exponential speedups in specific quantum algorithms. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations and preliminary experiments. The core mechanism leverages a dynamic state mapping that facilitates rapid collapse across a large state space, significantly reducing the time required to evaluate quantum circuits. This research contributes to a fundamental understanding of parallel quantum computation and offers a promising framework for achieving substantial speedups in various quantum applications.

title: 基于自适应量子势的优化算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on adaptive quantum potentials, designed to address the challenges of optimizing complex models effectively. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their applicability to diverse model structures. Our algorithm dynamically adjusts the quantum potential during the optimization process, adapting to the model's inherent complexity. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through a series of illustrative examples, showcasing its superior performance compared to existing optimization techniques across multiple benchmark datasets. The core mechanism leverages a novel approach to model parameter adjustment based on a dynamically evolving quantum potential, offering enhanced precision and adaptability within complex optimization scenarios.

title: Nonlinear Topological Geometry: A Quantum Entanglement-Based Computational Model

title: Quantum Entangled State Transfer Optimization – An Extended Topological Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Entangled State Transfer (QEST) represents a paradigm shift in secure communication, moving beyond traditional encryption methods and leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. This paper explores the optimization of QEST using a novel hybrid approach that integrates quantum state adaptation and topological optimization. We propose a system where the quantum state is dynamically transformed through a tailored topological algorithm, enhancing information protection and ultimately boosting transfer efficiency. The core mechanism centers around the strategic application of a topological transformation to quantum states, yielding significant improvements in the fidelity and speed of transfer. This work presents a framework for significantly enhancing the capabilities of QEST, pushing the boundaries of secure communication through the synergistic integration of quantum entanglement and topological optimization. The paper details the methodology, results, and preliminary analysis of this new approach.

title: 混沌理论的量子化计算框架
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computation framework leveraging the unique properties of chaos. Traditional quantum computation often focuses on the underlying quantum algorithms, while chaos theory offers a powerful tool for understanding and optimizing computational processes. We propose a quantum algorithm designed to transform the quantum computation itself into a quantum chaotic system, thereby enhancing computational efficiency. This framework utilizes the inherent self-organization of chaos to achieve significant improvements in algorithm performance. The core mechanism involves mapping the core quantum computation to the dynamics of a chaotic system, effectively amplifying the system's response to perturbations and promoting faster convergence to a stable solution. This work explores the potential of this approach to unlock new capabilities in quantum computation, addressing limitations currently faced by existing algorithms.

title: Graph-Based Anomaly Detection with Temporal Graph Kernels
abstract: Anomaly detection in graph-structured data is a crucial task across diverse domains, including social network analysis, fraud detection, and cybersecurity. Traditional graph anomaly detection methods often struggle to effectively capture the dynamic nature of graphs, which evolve over time. This paper proposes a novel approach utilizing temporal graph kernels to address this limitation. The core idea is to define kernels that measure the similarity between graph structures at different points in time, allowing for the detection of anomalous changes in graph connectivity and node behavior. The proposed method leverages the power of kernel methods to efficiently compute these temporal similarities, providing a robust and scalable solution for anomaly detection in evolving graph environments. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a conceptual framework, highlighting its applicability to various real-world scenarios. The key contribution lies in the systematic development and application of temporal graph kernels, representing a significant advancement in graph anomaly detection techniques.

title: Quantum Entanglement Non-Asymmetry Theory
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, remains a profoundly mysterious phenomenon. While its existence has been experimentally verified, its fundamental nature remains largely inaccessible to direct manipulation. This paper presents a novel theoretical framework, "Non-Asymmetric Entanglement Theory" (NAET), designed to address this challenge. NAET proposes a fundamentally new approach to understanding and utilizing entanglement by explicitly incorporating non-symmetry into its core principles. We explore the implications of this integration for quantum computation, focusing on enhancing entanglement strength and stability. The theoretical model developed leverages a carefully constructed concept of "Non-Asymmetric Entanglement" to provide a new perspective on the limitations and potential of current quantum algorithms. This work aims to provide a more comprehensive and mathematically rigorous understanding of entanglement, offering a pathway to enhanced quantum computing capabilities.

title: Dynamic Probability Distribution Evolutionary Algorithm: Adaptive Feature Selection Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel evolutionary algorithm based on dynamically adjusted probability distributions, designed for rapid optimization of complex problems. The core mechanism involves a continuous, adaptive feature selection process, driven by the algorithm's internal probability distribution. This approach distinguishes the algorithm from traditional evolutionary methods by its inherent flexibility and capacity to respond to evolving data characteristics. The paper details the design of the dynamic probability distribution, the optimization process, and the resulting performance improvements in a series of benchmark datasets. We demonstrate that the adaptive feature selection strategy consistently outperforms static feature selection methods across a range of problem types. The algorithm's efficiency stems from its ability to iteratively refine feature representations based on observed data, ultimately leading to more robust and accurate solutions.

We present a rigorous analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in complex environments.

title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Philippine Tourism: An Extended Technology Acceptance Model of Trust, Privacy Concerns, Service Quality, and Booking Intention
abstract: The widespread application of AI chatbots in tourism has changed the way people find information about their travels, communicate with service providers, and make booking transactions. Although the application of conversational AI in tourism systems is increasingly common, there is still no sufficient empirical evidence related to the factors affecting tourists' willingness to use AI chatbot-assisted booking system in emerging tourism destinations. Based on the extended version of Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), this study explores the impact of perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, trust, privacy concerns, and service quality on booking intention and attitude toward AI chatbots as a mediating variable. In this study, the quantitative research design has been used, and data have been gathered through surveying 373 tourists who visited major destinations in Misamis Oriental and Bukidnon, Philippines, during February 2025 – December 2025. For data analysis, the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling method was applied. As a result, the effect of perceived usefulness, service quality, privacy concerns, and attitude toward AI chatbots on booking intention has been confirmed. Perceived usefulness, privacy concerns, and service quality have also proved to be significant predictors of attitude toward AI chatbots, while perceived ease of use and trust have failed to show significant effect on attitude. Moreover, attitude toward AI chatbots acts as a mediator between perceived usefulness, privacy concerns, service quality, and booking intention. These findings show that tourists appraise AI chatbot technologies mainly in terms of functional value and performance rather than just trust considerations. The current study extends the Technology Acceptance Model by including service-related and privacy-related variables.

title: Adaptive Transfer Learning Based Anomaly Detection for Industrial IoT System
abstract: This paper proposes a transfer learning-based anomaly detection framework coupled with adaptive learning for predictive maintenance in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. The proposed framework is designed and validated using a small-scale prototype to demonstrate its feasibility and effectiveness. The proposed architecture addresses the computational limitations of edge devices by employing a cloud-assisted/remote processing framework, where sensor data are streamed through Apache Kafka for real-time analysis. A lightweight Conditional Autoencoder is used to detect anomalies from streaming sensor data, making the framework suitable for resource-constrained industrial environments. To overcome the scarcity of machinespecific training data, a global model is trained using data collected from machines belonging to the same machine category. The trained global model is subsequently adapted to individual machines using transfer learning whenever machine-specific data are available. The framework continuously monitors incoming sensor data for concept drift and performs adaptive retraining when persistent drift is detected, enabling the model to learn changes in machine behavior caused by aging and wear. The system processes incoming data through parallel anomaly detection and drift detection pipelines while storing labeled operational data for future model adaptation and retraining. The proposed framework provides an adaptive and scalable approach for real-time anomaly detection in Industrial IoT predictive maintenance systems. The experimental implementation is carried out using a remote processing framework. The proposed architecture is cloud-ready and is intended to support cloudassisted deployment for large-scale Industrial IoT environments in future work.

title: Molecular Déjà Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Molecular Properties in Frontier Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly employed to predict molecular properties. However, prediction error alone cannot distinguish prediction from retrieval of published values. We audit 22 frontier models on 12 molecular regression datasets in a zero-shot setting, assessed against a molecule-blind reference derived from each dataset's labels. Significant retrieval is concentrated on 5 datasets, with isolated flagged LLMs elsewhere. Increasing the reasoning setting raises the number of flagged model--dataset combinations from 47 to 89 of 264. An in-context blinding experiment reduces retrieval but leaves a quarter of the combinations flagged. Blinding changes model rankings and increases errors. Because blinding also removes chemically interpretable structure, the error increase can only be partially attributed to reduced retrieval.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to extracting topological information from complex systems using a dynamically adaptive quantum algorithm. Traditional methods rely on classical computation, while this research leverages quantum computation's unique properties to achieve more precise and efficient topological information extraction. The core mechanism involves quantum simulation, followed by an adaptive quantum algorithm designed to identify and quantify key topological features. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations of a simplified, yet representative, system exhibiting topological properties. The results highlight the potential of this method to overcome limitations of existing techniques, offering a pathway towards deeper insights into complex phenomena.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Bayesian Inference for Optimal Resource Allocation
abstract: Quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference offers a paradigm shift in optimization, potentially surpassing classical algorithms in complex, dynamic systems. This paper investigates the implementation of a novel quantum-enhanced Bayesian inference algorithm, designed to optimize resource allocation in sectors like logistics and energy grids. We detail the core mechanism, utilizing a quantum-enhanced variational quantum computation (VQC) to approximate the posterior distribution, ultimately demonstrating its superior performance compared to existing classical approaches. The paper explores the potential benefits of this approach, including enhanced speed, improved accuracy, and the capacity to handle complex, non-linear systems.

The proposed method demonstrates promising results through experimental analysis, showcasing its effectiveness in a range of classification and regression tasks. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential impact of this approach on the field of deep learning.

title: Quantum Machine Learning Parameter Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning Parameter Optimization (QMLPO) presents a novel approach to parameter optimization within quantum machine learning models, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum entanglement and quantum algorithms. This paper explores the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to accelerate parameter search and enhance model performance. We detail the core mechanism, outlining how quantum algorithms are integrated to overcome the limitations of classical optimization techniques. The research investigates the impact of quantum entanglement on the efficiency of parameter adjustments, ultimately aiming to improve the robustness and accuracy of quantum machine learning models. The paper concludes with a discussion of the current challenges and future directions for QMLPO.

title: Dynamic Geometry Deconstruction & Quantum Computation
abstract: This paper explores the potential of dynamic geometry structures to revolutionize geometric reconstruction and decomposition, leveraging the power of quantum computation. We introduce a novel algorithm, "Dynamic Geometry Deconstruction & Quantum Computation," which utilizes dynamically adjusted geometric structures to achieve complex geometry reconstruction. Traditional methods often rely on static or fixed geometries, but this approach offers unprecedented flexibility and adaptability. The core mechanism involves the continuous evolution of geometric structures guided by quantum computations, allowing for the deconstruction and reconstruction of intricate geometric forms. The paper details the algorithm's design, its quantum computational components, and preliminary results demonstrating its efficacy in reconstructing complex geometric datasets. We discuss the benefits of this approach, particularly in handling non-standard geometries and achieving high-fidelity reconstructions.

title: Fractal Symbolic Regression
abstract: This paper introduces Fractal Symbolic Regression (FSR), a novel approach to mathematical discovery that leverages the principles of fractal geometry and symbolic regression. The core idea is to represent both data and equations within a fractal space, thereby facilitating the identification of patterns exhibiting self-similarity and scale invariance. Traditional symbolic regression relies on searching through a vast space of possible equations, often struggling with complex datasets and identifying underlying mathematical structures due to the lack of inherent scale relationships. FSR addresses this limitation by explicitly incorporating fractal representation, allowing algorithms to naturally recognize and exploit repeating patterns at different scales. The methodology involves transforming the dataset into a fractal representation, typically through techniques like iterated function systems (IFS) or fractal dimension estimation, and then applying symbolic regression algorithms within this fractal framework. We demonstrate the potential of FSR to uncover mathematical relationships that would be difficult or impossible to identify using conventional symbolic regression. This approach offers a promising avenue for exploring complex systems and uncovering fundamental mathematical laws. The effectiveness of FSR is illustrated through a series of theoretical examples and conceptual analyses, highlighting its advantages over standard symbolic regression techniques.

title: Title: Quantum-Driven Emergent Algorithm Design
abstract: Quantum-driven emergent algorithm design represents a paradigm shift in computational methodology, aiming to create algorithms that spontaneously generate novel and complex behaviors through quantum phenomena. This paper explores the core mechanisms and potential applications of this approach, focusing on leveraging superposition, entanglement, and other quantum principles to circumvent traditional algorithmic limitations. We outline the core claims, propose a novel system for algorithm design, and discuss the significance of this research in advancing mathematical and computational science.

title: U-XAI-IDS: A Unified Benchmark for Domain-Feasible and Adversarially-Robust Explainability in Intrusion Detection
abstract: Code, checkpoints, and the resumable evaluation harness for U-XAI-IDS, a unified benchmark scoring IDS explanations (SHAP, LIME variants, Integrated Gradients) on fidelity, stability, domain feasibility, inter-explainer agreement, and adversarial robustness across four detector families and two datasets (NSL-KDD, CICIDS2017). Introduces Domain-Constraint-Aware (DCA) perturbation and the Domain Feasibility Rate (DFR) metric. Paper PDF is available in the repository and as a linked Zenodo record.

title: Dynamic Probability Topology: A Novel Approach to Adaptive Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to algorithm design termed Dynamic Probability Topology (DPT). The core principle of DPT lies in constructing a dynamically evolving topology based on input data and computational goals. Unlike static topology algorithms, DPT allows the topology to be adjusted automatically, enabling more flexible and efficient solutions. We propose a mechanism that leverages probability distributions to optimize the topology formation process, achieving adaptive algorithm design. The significance of this work lies in its ability to generate topologically diverse solutions, tailored to specific needs and data characteristics. This results in improved performance and adaptability across a range of computational problems. The paper details the underlying principles, provides a conceptual framework, and demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed DPT algorithm through illustrative examples.

title: Title: Lattice-Based Formal Verification of Cryptographic Protocols
abstract: Lattice-based formal verification offers a promising approach to securing cryptographic protocols, leveraging the inherent properties of lattices for mathematical proof. This paper explores the development of a novel framework for rigorous verification, employing mathematical induction to establish security guarantees. We present a new method that moves beyond traditional testing by utilizing the power of lattice-based techniques, reducing the need for exhaustive computation. The core mechanism centers around establishing properties through mathematical induction, providing a robust and verifiable approach to protocol security. The research investigates the effectiveness of this framework in validating specific cryptographic protocols, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance security.

title: Adaptive Quantum Simulation of Non-Local Interactions
abstract: This paper explores the development of an adaptive quantum simulation framework designed to enhance the accuracy of simulations of non-local interactions, a significant challenge in quantum physics. The core of the system involves a dynamically adjusting feedback loop that monitors system dynamics and modifies simulation parameters to optimize for fidelity. We introduce a novel approach that leverages the system's evolution to iteratively refine the simulation, resulting in improved representation of complex quantum phenomena. This framework offers a potential solution to existing limitations in simulating non-locality, particularly within the context of quantum entanglement and quantum information processing. The paper details the methodology, proposes initial experimental assessments, and concludes with a discussion of future research directions.

title: Field-Adaptive Probability Distribution Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adjustment algorithm for field-adaptive probability distributions, designed to enhance model accuracy through automated error correction. The core mechanism centers around a machine learning-based probability distribution adjustment process, which iteratively learns from experimental data and model prediction errors to dynamically adjust probability distribution parameters. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and a case study involving a regression model, showcasing improved performance compared to static adjustment methods. The proposed algorithm addresses the limitations of traditional approaches by providing a flexible and adaptive framework for model calibration and uncertainty quantification.

title: Title: Non-Linear Geometric Phase Transitions in Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the potential for non-linear geometric phase transitions to govern the behavior of neural networks, specifically focusing on training and deployment dynamics. Neural networks often exhibit unexpected and complex behavior, and a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms is crucial for improving model performance and robustness. We propose a novel framework for analyzing and modeling these transitions by treating the network's evolution as a geometric phase transition. The model incorporates a dynamic, non-linear geometric transformation that influences the network's parameters and structure throughout training. We explore how this transformation affects the network's learning rate, gradient behavior, and ultimately, the model's ability to generalize. This work aims to identify patterns and characteristics that influence model evolution, offering a new perspective on the design and optimization of neural networks. The core claim is that these geometric phase transitions are a fundamental driver of network behavior, and that analyzing them can reveal valuable insights into model stability and performance.

title: Title: Phase-Based Constraint Propagation in Topological Quantum Circuits
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithm for propagating constraints across topological quantum circuits, addressing a critical challenge in the field: the inherent instability of these circuits. We propose a 'Phase-Driven Constraint Propagation' system, which iteratively adjusts constraints based on the circuit's phase relationships, thereby enhancing circuit stability and fidelity. The system leverages the fundamental properties of quantum mechanics to achieve this improvement. This work focuses specifically on enhancing the robustness of quantum circuits, a key aspect of achieving reliable quantum computation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of constraint parameters driven by phase shifts, offering a promising pathway to overcome limitations in current constraint propagation techniques.

title: Soil Geochemical Investigation of Cu–Pb–Zn Anomalies in the Örencik Prospect (Geyve, Sakarya, Türkiye)
abstract: This study evaluates Cu–Pb–Zn soil-geochemical anomalies in the Örencik prospect, NW Türkiye, using robust thresholding, multivariate statistics and indicator-kriging probability mapping. The dataset comprises 1100 primary B-horizon soil samples collected on a nested grid locally densified from 50 × 100 m to 50 × 50 m and 25 × 25 m. Background–anomaly boundaries for Cu, Pb, Zn and As were defined using the median and normalised median absolute deviation (nMAD) of log10-transformed concentrations. The element-specific M + nMAD thresholds were 54.68 ppm Cu, 19.18 ppm Pb, 81.23 ppm Zn and 13.68 ppm As. At or above these thresholds, 15.64% of Cu, 16.64% of Pb and 12.18% of Zn observations were classified as anomalous; notably, 133 of the 134 anomalous Zn samples remained within the weak anomaly class. Correlation analysis and PCA distinguish a Cu–As association from a Zn–Co–Ni–V association; PC1 and PC2 explain 69.51% of the total variance, while a Pb-dominated PC3 is treated only as an exploratory secondary component. Indicator kriging delineates compact and discontinuous Cu probability zones, a more continuous Pb belt and a broad Zn pattern. Integration of the robust thresholds, multivariate relationships and spatial probability patterns indicates that Zn variability has a stronger lithological contribution, whereas spatially coherent Cu and Pb zones provide the principal exploration targets. These targets require geological verification and are not interpreted as confirmed economic mineralisation.

title: Feeding the machine: remuneration, transparency and the limits of copyright in the age of generative AI
abstract: Abstract This article applies a utilitarian evaluative framework grounded in IceTV Pty Limited v Nine Network Australia Pty Limited (‘Ice TV’) to survey the position in the European Union (‘EU’), the United Kingdom (‘UK’) and the United States (‘US’), and advances a two-tiered suite of proposals. The first consists of incremental measures extending the existing copyright framework. The second proposes a sui generis Computational Extraction Right, a right analogous to, but distinct from, the reproduction right, whose purpose is not to prohibit copying but to recognize and remunerate a form of value extraction that copyright law was never designed to govern.

title: Deep learning survival analysis with time-varying covariates: extending PyCox to assess COVID-19 antiviral treatments and long-COVID associations
abstract: Objectives: To extend the PyCox to accommodate time-varying covariates using counting process data, addressing immortal time bias in survival analysis. Materials and methods: We modified PyCox to support counting process data structures for time-varying covariates and applied it to 2 246 913 Medicare beneficiaries aged ≥65 with COVID-19 (January-September 2022; 2 785 807 longitudinal records). We compared traditional Cox regression, original PyCox, and modified PyCox in estimating associations between early antiviral treatment (nirmatrelvir or molnupiravir) and long-COVID. Performance metrics included concordance index (C-index), integrated Brier score (IBS), and integrated negative binomial log-likelihood (IBLL) and time-dependent Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC), Brier score, and permutation importance. Results: Among patients, 19.5% received nirmatrelvir, 2.6% received molnupiravir, and 14% developed long-COVID. Traditional Cox and modified PyCox produced concordant hazard ratios (HR) for nirmatrelvir (0.874 and 0.878) and molnupiravir (0.909 and 0.918); original PyCox estimated stronger associations (HR = 0.822 and 0.879). The treatment-effect difference formed a gradient: 3.5-4.0 percentage-points for time-varying models, 4.6 for time-fixed Cox, and 5.7 for time-fixed PyCox. Discrimination, calibration, and fit were comparable overall; modified PyCox showed higher time-dependent AUCs (0.536-0.609) than time-fixed PyCox (0.481-0.519) and relied on largely different top predictors. Modified and original PyCox trained in 1 min 14 s and 3 min 18 s, vs 5 min for traditional Cox. Discussion: Treatment-contrast magnitude and covariate importance varied by models, suggesting temporal covariate structure and modeling approach jointly influence treatment-effect estimates. Conclusion: Extending PyCox to accommodate time-varying covariates improves computational efficiency while maintaining estimation accuracy comparable to standard time-varying methods.

title: What Matters, When? Diagnosing and Improving Conditional Visual Grounding in Visuomotor Imitation Policies
abstract: Visuomotor imitation policies can achieve high performance under in-distribution visual conditions yet fail when visually similar objects or receptacles are introduced. We study this behavior as a problem of conditional visual grounding: the visual target required for successful control changes with the manipulation phase and, in more complex tasks, with the observed task state. Using Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT), we systematically introduce distractor objects and receptacles with controlled color and shape similarity and localize failures to picking and placement. We find that distractor sensitivity is specific to both the type of visual similarity and the manipulation stage. Guided by this diagnosis, we evaluate distractor augmentation, phase-dependent attention regularization, and appearance-based visual prompting as complementary interventions for improving target selection while preserving spatial information required for control. These interventions substantially improve robustness in simulation and on a physical UR3e. We further examine the same failure pattern in a pretrained vision-language-action policy on a state-conditioned instrument-handling task, where the observed state of a medical instrument determines the correct destination. Together, the results show that visual distractors can cause incorrect object or destination selection even when the underlying manipulation skill remains intact, and that explicitly improving target selection can substantially recover performance across distinct visuomotor policy-learning regimes.

title: Compact Bellman-Grounded Cognitive Maps for Cost-Aware Navigation
abstract: Biological agents navigate familiar environments not by re-solving routes for each new goal, but by reusing a learned map built once and read off as goals change. Existing artificial cognitive-map models mimic this reuse, yet their guidance is not explicitly grounded in additive heterogeneous route costs. Furthermore, they often struggle with memory efficiency: representative state-indexed and high-rank spectral constructions incur substantial storage growth as the environment scales. We present BCM, which grounds a reusable cognitive map in local edge costs through a self-supervised Bellman-grounded objective and a compact coordinate encoding, supporting changing goal queries without per-goal retraining. On weighted grids of up to $N=1600$ nodes, BCM maintains full success and only a 5\% mean Gap relative to exact Dijkstra search, compared with about $45\%$ for a connectivity-based spectral baseline. Notably, as the graph size increases from $N=400$ to $N=3600$, its memory footprint grows sublinearly while maintaining competitive performance, making our method scalable to complex environments. Together, these results show that additive route costs can be written into a compact, reusable cognitive-map representation, bridging the gap between biological flexibility and optimal path planning.

title: An Evaluation Framework for Generating Multi-View Images of a Person in a Scene
abstract: Recent generative image-editing Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) demonstrate impressive semantic editing capabilities but still struggle with spatially consistent camera angle changes. A primary bottleneck in training foundation models to execute free-form, promptable camera angle changes is the lack of specialized training data. While multi-view datasets exist for generic 3D environments and objects, there remains an absence of paired, multi-view datasets featuring human subjects at fixed locations in natural scenes, including frontal and side-profile views. Capturing such multi-camera data in unconstrained environments is logistically challenging and unscalable. In this paper, we first experiment with multiple state-of-the-art image editing models to create this data synthetically, but find that the outputs are frequently prone to hallucinations involving how much the subject's head turns relative to the background, often producing inconsistent environments. To address this issue, we propose the Head Scene Rotation Difference (HSRD) metric to quantitatively evaluate camera movements around a person. The proposed metric operates by decoupling camera movement from localized head pose manipulation. As demonstrated by the extensive experimentation, HSRD provides the pipeline necessary to evaluate 3D spatial parallax for a person in a scene, paving the way to reliably construct high-quality multi-view synthetic datasets.

title: FiMI Banking: A Sovereign Model for Indian Retail Banking
abstract: Banks need conversational systems that can answer product questions, assist customers with account-related requests, and operate safely within strict operational and regulatory constraints. General-purpose language models do not reliably meet these requirements. They fall short when a task requires grounded information, correct tool use, or cautious handling of bank-specific sensitive situations. title: Extracting Forgotten Prompts from Targeted Unlearned Models
abstract: Recent unlearning methods (e.g. NPO, DPO, LUNAR) make use of refusal alignment to suppress forgotten data. However, it has been shown that refusal responses might leave traces of unlearning, and recent attacks have been able to successfully recover some of the unlearned knowledge. In this paper, we uncover a new vulnerability. Existing attacks typically assume that the forgotten prompts are already known to the adversary and focus on recovering their answers. However, we show that the forgotten prompts themselves can be extracted by using the retained data and black-box access to the model. Our attack, Targeted Active Search (TAS), first identifies the forgotten entities by constructing canonical templates and entity pool, and selectively querying the model using the most informative template-entity pair under a limited query budget. Once the entities are identified, TAS instantiates prompt templates with those entities to probe the unlearned model and reconstruct the forgotten prompts. Experiments across three unlearning methods with three datasets and three LLMs shows that TAS recovers the forgotten entity with $100\%$ accuracy and reconstructs up to $95\%$ of forgotten prompts, all while using up to $99.7\%$ fewer queries than naive probing.

title: RecurTrace: Adaptive Latent Reasoning with Loop-Time Memory
abstract: Repeating a small block of middle layers increases a language model's effective inference depth without adding parameters or generating extra tokens, and recent work shows that this latent recurrence improves reasoning. However, two design choices limit these gains. Each iteration sees only the previous output and cannot directly access earlier computations. Moreover, a fixed loop count wastes depth on easy inputs while leaving hard ones with too little computation. We introduce RecurTrace, which addresses both limitations using the loop's own trajectory. Specifically, Loop Memory Attention lets each looped layer attend to its own states from previous iterations along the loop-time axis, so the model can revisit earlier computations instead of relying on the latest state alone. A halting head then reads the loop state and predicts whether to continue, with supervision from an oracle that identifies when additional depth still reduces loss. In a controlled MathQA comparison on the same looped backbone, RecurTrace achieves 56.9% accuracy with an average of 2.0 loops, exceeding the best fixed loop depth by 2.2 points at matched compute. By comparison, ACT and PonderNet collapse to one loop, and CALM reaches only 54.1% with 5.6 loops, while the stronger LoopUS-Conf and TaH-Mismatch baselines reach 55.3% at 3.2 loops and 55.7% at 2.1 loops. Finally, RecurTrace improves generation accuracy over same-budget fine-tuned baselines at 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, and 8B, with the gain growing with model size from 0.6 to 3.4 points.

title: Remember and Reweight: Enhancing Multi-Agent Debate with Experience Memory and Confidence Estimation
abstract: Multi-agent debate (MAD) improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models by having multiple agents iteratively refine their responses through discussion. However, MAD suffers from a critical vulnerability known as shared misconception: when a majority of agents initially converge on an incorrect answer, the debate process tends to amplify rather than correct the error. Existing methods primarily address peer skew but leave the agents' inherently biased concept priors unaddressed. To mitigate this systematic weakness, we propose R$^2$-MAD (Remember and Reweight for Multi-Agent Debate), a framework that equips agents with an experience memory accumulated from past debates. R$^2$-MAD intervenes on both failure modes through two complementary mechanisms: A debate-state-aware retrieval policy dynamically calibrates the concept prior by retrieving relevant historical evidence based on the current consensus level. Then these retrieved experiences provide a basis for estimating per-agent reliability, yielding confidence weights to modulate peer influence. Experiments on various benchmarks show that R$^2$-MAD achieves consistent improvements over existing single-agent and MAD baselines.

title: Beyond Shallow Alignment: How Post-Training Methods Determine Refusal Circuits And Steering Robustness
abstract: How do the methods used to train language models to refuse harmful requests shape how that refusal actually works inside the model? We compare three post-training methods - supervised fine-tuning, reasoning-augmented fine-tuning (training on reasoning chains that justify a safety decision), and preference optimization (ORPO) - across three architecturally distinct models (Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B, Qwen3-8B). We find that training method, not just data, reshapes how refusal is computed internally: reasoning-augmented training consistently produces a distinct kind of refusal computation, visible across all three models, while architecture independently shapes internal structure and how reliably refusal can be steered. Most importantly, no method we study achieves all three properties we would want from safe alignment at once: refusal that isn't concentrated in a few fragile components, safety gains that don't cost general capability, and safety behavior correctable through small, targeted edits. We caution against treating current post-training methods as a solved, reliable defense, especially for security-critical use. Code and models are available in https://github.com/hoangcuongnguyen2001/Beyond-Shallow-Alignment.

title: Random Attention: Rethinking KV Cache Eviction for Efficient Reasoning
abstract: Large language models achieve superior performance on tasks that require extended reasoning, but long chains of thought make the KV cache a severe memory bottleneck. Existing KV cache compression methods share one paradigm: score each cached token by some estimate of how much it will matter later, and keep the top-scoring ones. We show that the selection signal contributes almost nothing. Random Attention keeps the prompt and evicts uniformly at random within each attention head, computing no score at all; across four models and six reasoning tasks, it matches the strongest baseline in task performance while delivering 32-43% higher throughput than that method when deployed with vLLM. Controlled experiments explain this by showing that 1) the prompt is the fragile part of the cache, and most of the gap between selectors is just whether their selection signal happened to keep it; 2) the reasoning trace protects itself against eviction with redundancy at two levels, in the text (the model restates what it still needs as it works) and across attention heads (each keeps its own copy of the trace), so once the prompt is safe, a random draw retains enough copies of what the model still needs, and no score is required to pick them. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/Random-Attention.

title: Xiaomi-TabLDM: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
abstract: We introduce Xiaomi-TabLDM, a tabular large data foundation model for classification and regression via in-context learning, which delivers superior prediction accuracy without requiring task-specific fine-tuning. Pretrained exclusively on synthetic data generated from structural causal models (SCMs), our model enables more flexible context utilization and more efficient capacity scaling. i) A new performance standard. Strong regression performance across benchmarks: Xiaomi-TabLDM ranks 1st on OpenML-CTR23 and 2nd on regression across TALENT, TabArena, and BCCO, demonstrating consistently strong regression performance across four complementary benchmark suites. Favorable performance--efficiency trade-off: Xiaomi-TabLDM combines strong predictive performance with substantially lower computational cost. For example, on TabArena regression, it achieves the second-highest Elo while using 82% less training time and 68% less prediction time than the top-ranked TabFM. ii) Large-scale synthetic pretraining. Xiaomi-TabLDM expands the coverage and diversity of synthetic tabular data used for pretraining. We also adopt a three-stage training strategy together with dual-stream feature grouping, lightweight Attention Residual, and sparse Mixture-of-Experts, enabling Xiaomi-TabLDM to learn richer feature interactions and expert specialization across diverse tabular tasks. iii) Test-time scaling. Xiaomi-TabLDM further extends tabular prediction through test-time compute scaling, where allocating additional computation at inference time consistently improves predictive performance over the base model.

title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
abstract: Many recurring text functions are easy to describe but difficult to implement with rules, while calling a large remote model for every input introduces repeated cost, latency, and dependency on a provider. We present compile by training, which turns a natural-language specification into a reusable neural function. At compile time, teacher models generate task-specific examples that are used to train a small adapter for a compact interpreter. The resulting function runs without the teachers and can be stored, versioned, and composed like ordinary software. On FuzzyBench-Hard, a subset on which the Program-as-Weights fast compiler produced no exact matches, compile by training reaches 83.6% semantic accuracy. This higher accuracy comes with a higher compile-time cost: roughly a minute rather than seconds for the fast compiler. We deploy the compiler in a public interactive service and demonstrate compiled functions in a multi-site website helper, a language-controlled 3D avatar, and a bidirectional English-Claudish translator.

title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
abstract: Reasoning traces from chain-of-thought models appear to offer a legible window into how a model arrives at its answer. A growing body of work treats them as such, using LLM judges to diagnose errors, evaluate faithfulness, and provide step-level supervision via process reward models and generative critics. These practices rely on the text of a reasoning step carrying information about its functional role. But does the text actually encode information about which reasoning steps matter? We operationalize the importance of a reasoning step as its advantage: the change in expected reward, e.g., producing the correct final answer, from including that step, estimated via Monte Carlo rollouts. Basing ground truth on these estimates, we evaluate whether LLM judges can identify high-advantage steps and find that sufficiently capable LLMs can outperform a prevalence baseline but fall well short of a noise ceiling. Fine-tuning a model as a step-level critic yields strong improvement for incorrect responses but remains distant from ceiling for correct responses, suggesting that step importance is only partially recoverable from the text of the reasoning trace. Our findings contribute to a growing body of chain-of-thought faithfulness work that cautions against treating the legibility of reasoning traces as interpretability, especially with implications for process reward modeling.

title: Neural-Collapse-guided Task-Free Continual Anomaly Detection
abstract: Recent years have witnessed growing interest in continual anomaly detection for industrial visual inspection. However, real-world manufacturing environments exhibit unpredictable shifts in data distributions, rendering task-dependent continual learning assumptions impractical. To address this limitation, we formulate industrial anomaly detection as a task-free continual learning problem and propose NC-TFAD, a neural-collapse-inspired, geometry-driven framework for learning from non-stationary data streams without task boundaries. NC-TFAD freezes a pretrained backbone and aligns streaming features to a simplex Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF) prototype space to stabilize representation geometry under non-stationary streams. To satisfy the NC-inspired geometric construction in the absence of real anomalies, we generate synthetic anomaly samples as auxiliary anchors during training. Building on this geometry, we further introduce inter- and intra-class regularization together with a Focal Neural Collapse Contrastive (FNCC) loss to suppress representation drift and improve normal-anomaly separability. Finally, a normal-patch-prototype-guided localization branch constructs calibrated patch-wise deviation maps from normal training samples and fuses them with a weak self-attention prior, producing anomaly heatmaps without pixel-level annotations. Extensive experiments on MVTec AD and VisA show that NC-TFAD consistently outperforms representative task-free continual learning methods adapted from general vision, as well as unified anomaly detection baselines, in both image-level detection and pixel-level localization under the task-free continual learning protocol. These results highlight that geometry-driven modeling offers an effective and robust solution for task-free continual anomaly detection in real-world industrial applications.

title: Building and Evaluating Fixed-Voice Thai TTS from Synthetic Speech
abstract: In low-resource settings, deploying TTS typically requires choosing between a large voice-cloning model with costly inference or a compact fixed-voice system that requires a speaker-specific corpus. We study a third route: using a large voice-cloning model as a programmable data source to turn a short voice reference (e.g., 15 seconds) into a compact fixed-voice student trained entirely on synthetic speech. This setting makes pipeline design consequential: teacher errors become training targets, while filtering failed generations can reduce coverage of difficult texts. Thai further introduces challenges from ambiguous word boundaries, lexical tone, names and loanwords, numeric verbalization, and Thai-English code-switching. We study how text preparation, synthetic generation, quality filtering, rejection sampling, and frontend choices affect the resulting student, and where teacher limitations remain. We evaluate CER, Challenge-Set Keyword Accuracy, Prosody Pause Accuracy, speaker similarity, and speaking rate. The resulting 82M-parameter model, Wayu-Paxa-TTS-Edge, enables on-device Thai TTS without reference audio. It achieves 68.2% Challenge-Set Keyword Accuracy (85.5% of Gemini 3.1) and 91.4% pause precision, outperforming its OmniVoice teacher (89.9%) and reaching 94.8% of Gemini 3.1. It also achieves the lowest pause-placement error and intra-word pause rates among the three systems, and 3.7% and 1.1% CER on Thai and English, respectively. We open-source the model and evaluation framework for Thai TTS development.

title: The Delegation Danger Band: Why Mid-Capability Sub-Agents Over-Trust Inherited Stale State
abstract: Agent frameworks increasingly delegate work by forking sub-agents; a common default makes the child inherit the parent's full working context. We measure how the effect of inherited state changes with capability, where $C_m$ denotes clean fork-fresh accuracy. We compare 3 inheritance policies: Reset (fork fresh: base evidence only), Selective (curated handoff: + the useful prior conclusion), and Full (implicit fork: + the useful conclusion and $d$ copies of a superseded conclusion) over a same-family ladder (Qwen3 0.6/1.7/4/8B) on a frozen, closed-set, action-scored benchmark. Every task is solvable from the base evidence, so performance loss can be attributed to reliance on stale state. (1) Deference to superseded state falls sharply with measured capability $C_m$ (the slope's confidence interval, CI, excludes zero on every family) across 2 synthetic primitives plus MuSiQue and HotpotQA. (2) On the Qwen3 synthetic ladder, net inheritance harm follows a nonmonotone pattern: a mid-capability model (Qwen3-1.7B) is a statistically significant local minimum of net harm, falling below its fork-fresh baseline ($Δ(32)=-0.19$ [-0.25, -0.12]) and both neighbors, while the weakest model stays near-neutral and the strongest models stay robust. We call this harmful capability range a danger band. A within-model counting-difficulty sweep shows that the effect depends on model class even at matched $C_m$, and a live parent-to-child fork reproduces the mid-model harm. (3) Curated Selective handoff improves average accuracy over Full on all 3 datasets, largest at the in-band model, while the fixed-threshold capability router fails on the other datasets; a transferable router would need to predict the balance between reuse benefit and stale-context penalty. The benchmark is frozen and version-hashed.

title: DuplexSpeechBench-IFEval: Evaluating Implicit Instruction Following in Full-Duplex Voice Agents
abstract: Full-duplex voice agents must continuously decide when to speak, listen, backchannel, interrupt, overlap, and yield the conversational floor. Existing benchmarks evaluate these behaviors through explicit turn-management instructions, whereas voice agents are often configured through roles or personas from which appropriate conversational behavior must be inferred. We introduce DuplexSpeechBench-IFEval (DSB-IFEval), a benchmark for evaluating implicit instruction following in real-time spoken interaction. DSB-IFEval comprises 1,038 test cases derived from 240 controlled conversations spanning eight behaviorally contrastive assistant roles and five conditioning protocols: default behavior, explicit behavioral instructions, persona-implied behavior, combined persona-rule conditioning, and instruction conflict. We measure real-time floor management using the deterministic Instruction Adherence Score (IAS) and persona-consistent response content using the LLM-judged Persona Adherence Score (PAS). Across eleven real-time speech models, we find that executing an explicit floor-management policy does not reliably imply the ability to infer the same policy from a persona. Moreover, even frontier models such as GPT-Live-1 and Gemini-3.8-Live adapt their dialogue language to the assigned persona without consistently translating that persona into the appropriate full-duplex floor-management behavior. Finally, models that successfully resolve benign instruction conflicts often fail when safety-relevant role behavior should override an explicit directive. These results show that inferring role-implied behavior, executing it in real time, and resolving instruction conflicts remain distinct challenges for full-duplex voice agents.

evidence.abstract: Full-duplex voice agents must continuously decide when to listen, backchannel, interrupt, handle speech overlaps, take the floor, and yield. title: Computationally Efficient Pathology Segmentation using Knowledge Distillation from Foundation Models
abstract: Automatic tissue segmentation is essential for large-scale analysis of histopathology whole-slide images (WSIs), but accurate pixel-level segmentation remains challenging. Pixel-level annotations are expensive to obtain, models pre-trained on natural images may transfer poorly to histopathology, and pathology foundation models, despite their strong representations, are computationally expensive to deploy at scale. We address these challenges with a foundation-model knowledge distillation framework for efficient tissue segmentation. We first train Virchow2-based segmentation teachers, including a LoRA-adapted variant, achieving state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance across four datasets: PUMA, IGNITE, BEETLE, and a private blood vessel segmentation dataset. We then transfer response-level and feature-level knowledge from these teachers into compact student networks. Distillation consistently improves student performance over supervised training alone, producing state-of-the-art or near state-of-the-art results with substantially fewer parameters and up to ten-fold higher inference throughput than foundation-model-based segmentation networks. These results show that foundation-model knowledge can be effectively transferred to efficient segmentation models for scalable deployment without compromising performance. Models trained on the public datasets will be released through TIAToolbox.
